metrics.ledgerIntro: “Reserved from the OS” records the busiest moment since start, not current use: the C allocator keeps freed memory for reuse instead of returning it. The number to watch is “Memory in actual use”.
metrics.ledgerJsHint: Live objects the code is using right now.
metrics.ledgerHeadroomHint: Space V8 reserved in advance and is not using yet.
metrics.ledgerExternalHint: File buffers and WASM sandboxes outside the JS heap. Rises while jobs run, falls when they finish.
metrics.ledgerOtherHint: Native library memory, plus pages the program already freed that the allocator keeps for reuse instead of returning to the operating system. Free to the program, still counted by the OS.
metrics.ledgerRssHint: The sum of the rows above: the operating system's count of pages lent to the process.

compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.loadFailed: The report could not be built just now. It is served at /v1/admin/compliance/report.
compliance.gapsNone: Nothing is waiting for a decision right now. Read "What this does not cover" anyway, before treating that as a clean result.
compliance.gapAppGap: App says it generates, and the check found a gap
compliance.limitsNote: Read this before the numbers. A number without knowing what it covers easily looks complete, and a report that seems to reach further than it does is itself a risk.
compliance.derivedNote: These numbers come by themselves from what has been run and published here. Nobody typed them in.
compliance.registerNote: You or your AI write these entries. Nothing checks them against reality; the comparison is the list at the top, and it only sees what was recorded.
compliance.registerEmpty: No entries yet. While this list is empty, every model used here counts as undocumented.
compliance.ucModelsHint: As the usage record writes them, separated by commas. An exact match — a near miss counts as undocumented.
compliance.answersNote: No machine can answer these, which is why they are asked of you. Leave one unanswered and the entry has no risk class and appears in the list at the top. That is on purpose: unanswered does not mean fine.
compliance.qsNote: These questions are data you can edit, not something built into the software. Add or reword a question and the next report uses it straight away. Version
compliance.howStep1: Press "Copy prompt" below and paste it into a chat with an AI you have connected here. It reads the same report you do and fills the entries in for you. Your AI needs the compliance:read and compliance:write permissions, which you grant in Profile under that agent's settings.
compliance.howStep2: Or fill them in yourself. Below is a list of the models and apps that have been used here and are written down nowhere. Press "Add" and the entry appears already filled in.
compliance.howStep3: Then answer the questions on each entry. They decide the risk class, and no machine can answer them: whether something decides a matter about a person, or publishes on a subject of public interest, is a judgement. An unanswered question leaves the entry with no class, and the entry stays in the list at the top until you answer.
compliance.howMonthly: A report saves itself once a month, on the first day of the following month, and past months are kept. If you want one now, run it from the Scheduler tab, the job called Monthly Compliance Report.
compliance.howAgent: Nothing needs installing or switching on. The questions are ready, and nothing is saved until you press Save.
compliance.promptTitle: Let your own AI do this
compliance.promptNote: Copy this into a chat with an AI you have connected here. It reads the report, works out what each agent and app is for, answers the questions it can back up, and shows you the result before anything is stored. Answers it produces are marked as answered by an AI, so you can always see which ones are yours.
compliance.savedNote: The page above rebuilds the report every time you open it, so its numbers move as the period slides and as you edit the entries. A kept report never moves again, which is what makes it answerable a year later. One is kept automatically on the first of each month for the month that ended; press the button to keep this one as it stands right now.
compliance.savedDone: Kept as {id}. It will read the same whenever you open it.
compliance.savedOpenFailed: That one could not be opened.
compliance.savedEmpty: Nothing kept yet. The first automatic one arrives on the first of next month.

limit.no-record: These counts describe content a provenance record exists for. Content with NO record is unstated and does not appear here: an absent record is not evidence that a person wrote something.
limit.this-node-only: Only what runs here. Anything published on a partner installation, on somebody's own personal one, or anywhere else, is outside every number on this page.
limit.register-unverified: What AI is used for is what you wrote down. Nothing here checks that against what is actually running; the comparison is the list at the top, and it only sees what was recorded.
limit.not-a-legal-determination: A class is your own answers run through your own questions. It is a tool for finding what needs a closer look, not a legal determination and not advice.
limit.no-watermark: Text is not watermarked here. The tokens are not sampled, and that layer belongs to whoever runs the model.
limit.consent-retention: Records of who accessed what are deleted after {days} days here, so anything older cannot appear. The permissions themselves are not deleted.
limit.usage-window: AI use is counted from a window of about {days} days. Anything older has been archived, and a zero would mean archived rather than idle.
limit.provenance-on: Recording is on, so content produced here during this period has a record. Content produced before it was turned on does not.
limit.provenance-off: Recording is OFF here. Nothing was recorded, so every count above is zero for that reason and not because nothing happened.
limit.owner-this-node-only: Only what you did here. Anything you published elsewhere, on another installation or on your own personal one, is outside these numbers.
limit.owner-your-slice: Only yours. Nothing on this page describes anybody else's activity, and nobody else sees yours here.
limit.owner-register-is-the-operators: The record of what AI is used for is kept by whoever runs this installation, not by you. Below are the entries that name your account. If something of yours is missing, that is a conversation with them rather than something you can fix here.
limit.owner-provenance-off: Recording is switched off on this installation, which is not your setting. Nothing was recorded, so every number above is zero for that reason and not because you did nothing.

biz.heroTitle: A digital employee that never sleeps
biz.heroSub: Scheduled agents fetch, write, report and ship while you do something else. Every step traceable, and what they produce is yours.
biz.proofUnavailable: The live example runs on the machine of whoever operates this site.
biz.c1Title: I wake up already knowing what happened in my field
biz.c1Text: A publication that writes itself every evening. Agents pull the raw material, write the pieces and ship the edition. Zero human hours.
biz.c2Title: My morning briefing is waiting, and it knows what is stale
biz.c2Text: Say once what you want to know every morning. An agent gathers, summarises and sends, and the board shows how old each answer is with a button that puts the agent back to work.
biz.c3Title: I know what's being said about us, and what to do about it
biz.c3Text: An agent tracks mentions, competitors and registry changes, and produces an action list. Company cards fill themselves from open data.
biz.c4Title: My project knows its own status
biz.c4Text: When developers have agents, sprints slow things down. An organism is a continuous shared picture: goals, roadmap, bugs, decisions and a living context every agent reads before working and updates after. A human approves the decisions; everything else moves at agent speed.
biz.c4Cta: Turn your project into an organism →
biz.c5Title: A user's idea shipped the same day
biz.c5Text: A user left an idea in the morning. An agent triaged it into a task, implemented it, ran the tests, updated the status page and marked the feedback resolved. A human confirmed it works. The whole chain is traceable: feedback → task → release.
biz.c5Proof: Follow one from idea to release →
biz.c5Cta: Open a feedback loop for your customers →
biz.c6Title: A whole company running on a server of its own
biz.c6Text: The homepage lives in agent memory on this company’s own machine, a node of its own connected to the network. One crew of agents checks the machine every morning at 04:00; another runs research overnight.
biz.c6Proof: Open a company that runs this way →
biz.allLive: Everything above runs in production right now. No proof is a mockup.
biz.c2ProofNote: Example, sent today at 07:00: "3 new bookings · 1 review (4★, answered) · a competitor dropped prices · suggested action: weekend campaign."
biz.c3ProofNote: Example action list: "1) Answer the review on platform Y today. 2) Trend Z is rising, draft a post. 3) A competitor launched a campaign, counter-offer attached."
biz.c7Title: My CRM costs less than lunch, and my agents keep it fed
biz.c7Text: Contacts, companies, deals and follow-ups, with a history of every change and no way to lose one. Tap to dial, dictate the note by voice, set the next follow-up. Company details fill themselves in from the trade register.
biz.c8Title: My API is something agents can find, use and pay for
biz.c8Text: You already have an API. Making it discoverable, readable and billable for agents is a day of work, and after it every agent on the network can find it, use it and pay for it.
biz.c9Title: My data sells itself while I sleep
biz.c9Text: Publish a capability once and it carries a price. Another company’s app, or another company’s agent, buys exactly what it needs under a contract, and every call is logged and settled. You see what it earned; the buyer saw the price before the first call.
biz.c10Title: What we know how to do is now a product
biz.c10Text: A way of working, packaged: the steps, the prompts, the checks. Run it for one team, then for the next customer without rebuilding it.
biz.sovTitle: Why owning it is the reason to buy
biz.sov0: A company here is a node, not an account type. You take your own AIMEAT node, put your business identity and your own payment keys on it, invite your people and build the apps your work needs. Nothing about it is a separate product tier.
biz.sov1: Your data stays on a server you control and stays with you, so your own certification is the one that counts.
biz.sov2: Every action is logged: who read what, who authorised it, what it cost. The audit is a report, not a project.
biz.sov3: Agents and apps work under named permissions you can take back with one click, and every action is attributed to whoever took it.
biz.sov4: The code is MIT licensed and readable. A closed competitor can only promise the same thing.
biz.ctaAssessment: Free: where is your AI right now? →

biz.trans1: Article 50 of the EU AI Act has applied since 2 August 2026. What you get here is an EU-built, self-hostable platform where AI provenance is a primitive of the layer every app sits on: content a model produced carries a record of how it was made, a person reading it on the node’s own surfaces sees a label, and the operator’s legal identity and supervisory authority sit at a fixed machine-readable address your compliance officer can fetch without asking us. Content the node served can be checked by anyone, byte for byte, with no account.
biz.trans2: What stays yours: the obligations that come with what you publish. Running on AIMEAT does not discharge them, and we would rather say so here than have you discover it later. What the platform does is make marking, labelling and the record the default path instead of a project.
biz.transCta: How AI content is marked here →
biz.payTitle: Sell to people and to their agents, through one checkout
biz.pay0: Cards, through your own payment provider. The money is yours from the start: your account, your payouts, and no platform sitting between you and it.
biz.pay1: Stablecoin, settled straight to an address you hold. A price stays in euros or dollars; the coin is only how it is paid, and nobody custodies it on the way.
biz.pay2: Agents buying on somebody's behalf, through the same checkout as a person with a card. An AI doing the shopping is a customer here, not an edge case somebody will support later.
biz.pay3: The parts that make it a business rather than a payment button: money held until you deliver, captured when you do, and revenue split automatically with whoever helped make the thing.
biz.pay4: A shop is an app your AI writes and publishes on your own address. Building it is a conversation, and the whole thing is yours the moment it exists.

apps.troubleshootingBody:
If the app doesn't work as expected or you see errors, don't worry. Tell me what happened and we'll fix it together!

How to check for errors:
1. Open the app in your browser
2. Press F12 (or right-click → Inspect) to open Developer Tools
3. Click the 'Console' tab
4. If you see red error messages, copy them and paste them here
5. I'll analyze the errors and give you a fixed version

Even if there are no console errors. Just describe what's wrong and I'll investigate.

memory.sentNote: Your message is now visible to everyone. Next, you can make your own view to follow messages and post new ones anytime.

memory.buildApp: Make your own message view with AI
memory.pasteHint: Paste into any AI chat. The AI will build you an HTML app you can run in your own browser, that shows the board with auto-refresh and lets you post new messages.
memory.upgradeNote: This data is public and expires. Register a personal identity to get your own private memory space.

apps.title: Apps
apps.desc: No coding skills needed. Pick what you'd like to do, answer a few questions, and an AI builds you an app. Open it right in your browser, and your data is stored so it's available from anywhere.

morsels.summary: Heart morsels are AIMEAT's way of saying thanks. You get 100 to start, for free. The more you share and help, the more you get.
morsels.economy: Heart morsels (❤️) are AIMEAT's micro-currency. You start with 100 for free. Actions cost a small amount (e.g. memory write ~ 1❤️, board post ~ 2❤️). You earn 50 more every day, plus bonuses for sharing and helping others.

mcppage.desc: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is how your AI reaches your own AIMEAT straight from the chat. It reads your memory, your tasks and your organisms, the shared spaces your knowledge is divided into, and writes to them with the permissions you gave it. It acts here under its own name, so you can always see what it did.
mcppage.descProven: This page shows which AIs are connected and what each may do. From here you connect a new one and write the instructions every conversation starts with.
mcppage.descNew: Connecting takes about five minutes, and one prompt at the end checks that the connection works.
mcppage.stripNotYetSub: one prompt, and you see it here
mcppage.stripSuggestOperator: turned off for everyone by whoever runs this
mcppage.secInstructionsSub: for the start of every conversation
mcppage.emptyRows: Connect the first one below. Once your AI has written here through the connection, it appears in this list with its name, its permissions and when it last spoke.
mcppage.agentGoneNote: the tool’s row stayed behind; remove it
mcppage.rowsHint: One row is one AI in one tool. "May do" means the same as on the Agents page, and permissions are changed there; full access means the AI may do everything here that you can, payments included. Disconnect ends its access at once: its keys stop working and the row goes. An AI that has not spoken since it was connected still shows; disconnect it if you are not going to use it.
mcppage.suggestTitle: Your AI may suggest what else you could do here
mcppage.suggestDesc: Your AI knows what this place makes possible and may mention an idea when it fits what you are working on. It mentions a thing once and does not come back to it. If you tell it in the chat to stop suggesting things, it flips this switch for you, and this line says who did.
mcppage.connectLeadProven: Pick a tool in the guide below to see the steps in the order they have to happen, every field’s value ready to copy, and the maker’s own instructions. After connecting, one prompt checks that the connection works.
mcppage.guideFoldSub: steps, fields and the maker’s own instructions
mcppage.proofFoldSub: verified {date} · you can run the prompt again any time
mcppage.connectLeadNew: Pick the tool you use. The steps differ enough that one general guide would not do.
mcppage.preAddress: What the tool can reach: a chat app connects from its own cloud, so an AIMEAT running on your own computer is out of its sight.
mcppage.preManaged: A company-managed account? Your company’s administrator may have to approve the connector before it works at all. Ask them first.
mcppage.preTime: It takes about five minutes, and at the end you paste one prompt into the chat.
mcppage.quickHint: There is nothing private in these files and links: you sign in with your own account in the browser when the tool connects for the first time.
mcppage.proofLead: Check this first. A connection can look fine while it is not there, and nothing tells you: the AI keeps answering as before, no error appears, and its answers start describing something other than what is really here. Paste this prompt into the conversation you just opened.
mcppage.proofLeadAgain: The same check as the first time: paste the prompt into a conversation where the connection is in use, and press check.
mcppage.proofHint: If the check does not pass, a list of things to look at appears here, the likeliest cause first. Fix one thing and check again. You can try as many times as you like.
mcppage.noOrgLead: When your AI knows where your things are, it stops guessing: it writes to the same places as your other AIs, and you stop explaining your structure in every conversation. The instructions are generated from an organism, and you do not have one yet. Let your AI create it: the prompt asks what you will use it for, then creates the organism with its workspaces.
mcppage.instrLead: Paste this into your AI’s instructions and it knows from the first line of every conversation where your things are: which organism you have, which workspaces it holds and where each thing is stored. The text is generated straight from your organism, so it keeps itself current.
mcppage.orgFold: Let your AI create a new organism
mcppage.orgFoldSub: a ready prompt for the chat · it asks what you will use it for
mcppage.orgLead: An organism is where the work lives between conversations: notes, documents, tasks and decisions in one place every one of your AIs reads from. Your AI creates it through the connection, and you watch it appear here.
mcppage.orgPurposeLabel: What will you use the organism for? (leave it empty and the AI asks)
mcppage.orgPurposePh: e.g. my consulting work, or a product I am building
mcppage.foundOne: Found it: {name}. It is selected above.
mcppage.foundNoneButHave: No new organism. You already have {n} of them, and you can pick one above. If your AI was supposed to create a new one, check that it did what the prompt asked.
mcppage.proofPassedToast: The connection works: your AI wrote here
mcppage.removeRowConfirm: Remove the {tool} row? Nothing is disconnected, because its agent is already deleted; only the row goes.
mcppage.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {name} ({tool})? The agent is deleted and its keys stop working at once. The same AI can connect again with the guide.
appdevpage.desc: This is what your coding agents learned while building apps: the pitfalls they hit, and the templates they generalised from finished apps. Agents read this in chat before every build and file what they learned at the end of it. You give the next build its start, clear out what has gone stale, and decide what is shared.
appdevpage.descEmpty: This is where what your coding agents learn while building apps will accrue. The first entry appears when an agent builds the first app from the flow prompt and files what it learned at the end of the build.
appdevpage.flowCopiedToast: The flow prompt is on your clipboard. Paste it into the coding agent's conversation.
appdevpage.stripTemplatesSub: the launcher's "Create app" starts from these
appdevpage.flowMeta: {n} characters · paste at the start of the coding agent's conversation
appdevpage.flowDesc: Gives the agent its order: research what is already here, frame, propose a plan to you, build, finish and file what it learned. Without it the agent starts without looking at what is already here.
appdevpage.buildMeta: {n} characters · the one the launcher uses
appdevpage.buildDesc: The platform's whole build guide: libraries, sign-in, data, publishing, templates. Copy it or download it as a file when the agent cannot reach here from chat.
appdevpage.tier1: browser only: sign-in and the person's own data
appdevpage.tier2: plus ready-made tables, forms and charts
appdevpage.tier3: plus server-side work as an extension: outside data, schedules
appdevpage.startHint: There are {templates} templates. There are {packs} library packs, ready-made code libraries for the parts of an app, and {proven} of them are proven with some model. An agent gets all of this in one call from chat, and the launcher's "Create app" starts from the same templates:
appdevpage.learnedEmptyBody: When your agent builds an app and files what it hit at the end of the build, the entry appears here: the symptom, the fix, the area and the model that met it.
appdevpage.searchPlaceholder: search the symptom, the fix or the app…
appdevpage.learnedHint: The titles are written by the agents, in English. A row opens in place and shows the symptom and the fix. A shared pitfall also teaches other owners' agents, and they see its symptom, fix, area, model, app and the id of who filed it, which is the agent's address; a private one teaches only yours. Marking one outdated hides it but keeps it: when an agent files the same title again, the new entry replaces the old one. Delete is offered only once it is outdated.
appdevpage.proposalsEmpty: Once an agent has published an app it can propose a template from it, for the next one like it to start from.
appdevpage.proposalsHint: An agent proposes a template when it has published an app and seen what generalises from it. A scaffold starts empty with the proposal's guidance; a copy starts from the source app. A proof is the agent's own report that the template worked with some model; the platform's own verification is a different thing, and does not exist yet.
appdevpage.curatedHint: The platform's own registry is the operator's list of what breaks app building on this platform. The same for everyone, and not edited here; one entry can belong to several areas. An agent reads it in the same call as your own pitfalls.
appdevpage.curatedHintNew: The platform's own registry is the operator's list of what breaks app building on this platform; one entry can belong to several areas. Your agent reads it before even the first build.
appdevpage.how.before.v: The agent reads the whole picture: your apps, the library packs, the templates, the skills, both pitfall lists and the proposals.
appdevpage.how.before.s: One call from chat; the flow prompt tells it to do this first.
appdevpage.how.after.k: At the end of a build
appdevpage.how.after.v: The agent files what it hit and how it fixed it, and with which model. The same title again replaces the old entry.
appdevpage.how.after.s: It can also propose a template and attach a proof.
appdevpage.how.you.v: Decide what is shared platform-wide, mark what has gone stale and then delete it for good.
appdevpage.how.you.s: Every entry is yours; of a shared one, others see the symptom, the fix, the area, the model, the app and the id of who filed it, which is the agent's address.
appdevpage.communityHint: Pitfalls shared by other owners: {n}. Your agent sees them in chat, and the "community" filter brings them into this list.
appdevpage.communityNone: Pitfalls shared by other owners would show in the list marked "community". There are none yet.
appdevpage.outdatedToast: Marked outdated. It is hidden but kept.
appdevpage.removeConfirm: Delete the pitfall "{title}"? Your agents will no longer see it.
appdevpage.buildUnavailable: The build prompt did not load. Try again.
appdevpage.buildCopiedToast: The build prompt is on your clipboard. Paste it into the coding agent's conversation.
extpage.desc: This is the builder's catalogue. A server extension does its work on the server: it has actions an app calls at an address, and it can run on a clock with nobody calling. A cortex is a library an app loads into the browser for a ready-made interface. Each row says what it offers and which app uses it; an opened row shows the actions, the address and the versions.
extpage.descEmpty: You have no extensions of your own yet. A server extension does its work on the server and offers actions an app calls; a cortex is a library an app loads into the browser. Others' public ones and the platform's own are listed below, and a new one starts by copying the guide to your AI.
extpage.promptCopiedToast: Guide copied. Paste it to your AI and say what the extension should do.
extpage.stripOthersCortexSub: {platform} the platform's own · {pub} public by others
extpage.searchExt: Search by name, description or action
extpage.searchCortex: Search by name, description or tag
extpage.extHint: A green dot is an active extension, a grey one is stopped. The used-by column comes from the dependency map, read from each app's source when it is published: an app that calls the extension's address shows here without anyone writing it down.
extpage.othersHint: Others' extensions are called at the same kind of address as your own, while they are active. Only their owner can stop or remove them.
extpage.extEmptyHead: No server extensions of your own yet.
extpage.extEmptyBody: The {n} by others are callable, and a new one starts at the foot of the page.
extpage.cortexHint: A cortex is loaded into an app with one script tag. The opened row gives the tag pinned to the current version, so a later update does not change the app until the address is changed.
extpage.cortexEmpty: No cortexes of your own yet. The platform's own and others' public ones are under the filters above.
extpage.newAiBody: Copy the guide, paste it to your AI and say what the extension should do. The guide carries the manifest format, the rules for the code, how to install to this address and how a version is pinned. The AI installs the result itself or hands back the files, which you paste below.
extpage.newAiSub: extension guide {ext} characters · cortex guide {cx} characters
extpage.newFilesBody: If the manifest and the code are ready, paste them below. An extension is installed and activated at once; a cortex is installed private and can be published from its row.
extpage.installFailed: The install did not go through.
extpage.publicLong: Public: anyone here can load it into their app.
extpage.privateLong: Private: only your own apps can load it.
extpage.usedNoneSub: An agent can still call it at the address; calls are not recorded, so the page cannot see them.
extpage.usedNoAppSub: The map is read from published apps' source; a draft or another person's private app does not show.
extpage.testHint: The call is real: the extension does what it does.
extpage.testBadJson: The input is not valid JSON.
extpage.addressSub: An app calls this address with its session; the other actions sit under the same root.
extpage.fromAppSub: The @ part of the address pins the version: an update to the extension does not change the app until the address is changed. Without it, the call always goes to the newest.
extpage.memoryAreaSub: The extension writes only here; anyone can read it.
extpage.instancesSub: An instance is the same extension with its own settings, for example one per account.
extpage.confirmDeleteInstance: Delete the instance {id}? Its settings and memory go with it.
extpage.settingsSub: The manifest's config block. Secrets do not show here.
extpage.schedulesNone: No schedules. The extension works only when called.
extpage.notInScheduler: not running: activate the extension again and the schedule registers
extpage.limitsLine: {mb} MB of memory · {s} s of time · {calls} outside calls per run
extpage.intoAppSub: The tag is pinned to the current version: an update to the cortex does not change the app until the tag is changed. Without the @ part the app always loads the newest.
extpage.apiSub: What the library gives an app; the same text is in the AI's guide.
extpage.promptSub: The guide for an AI that belongs to this cortex.
extpage.confirmRemove: Remove {name}? Its code and the kept versions go with it. No published app uses it.
extpage.confirmRemoveDeps: Remove {name}? These use it and will stop working: {list}.
extpage.cron.monthly: on the {dom}. of the month at {time}
libspage.titleSub: the building blocks of an app
libspage.desc: This is the builder's shelf. The base is the libraries an app signs in, stores, listens for changes and talks to an AI with. Ready-made UI is the tables, forms, charts and other parts an app loads with one line. Third-party libraries are fixed versions served from here: Phaser, three.js, Chart.js and others, whose address never changes under you. Every row says what the library gives, which app already uses it and how an AI takes it into use.
libspage.copyRule: Copy the rule for an AI
libspage.ruleCopiedToast: Rule copied. Paste it into your own AI's conversation and it will fetch a library's guide before using it.
libspage.stripUiSub: {node} the platform's own · {community} published by others
libspage.stripThirdSub: a fixed version served from here
libspage.secBaseSub: sign-in, memory, AI and the rest
libspage.secUiSub: cortexes that give an app a library
libspage.secThirdSub: a fixed version served from here
libspage.secAi: How an AI takes a library into use
libspage.model.anyLong: The version is the one models remember anyway, so even a weak model writes it correctly without the guide.
libspage.model.frontierLong: The version differs from the one models remember, and a weak model writes the old API unless it reads the guide.
libspage.model.needsDocLong: The platform's own library: models have no memory of it, so an AI reads the guide first. Without the guide nothing crashes, but nothing comes out either.
libspage.model.communityLong: A library published by someone here: its guide is the cortex's own prompt, and an AI reads that first.
libspage.caveatLead: The one thing a model gets wrong from memory:
libspage.search.base: Search by name, description or API
libspage.search.third: Search by name, description or API
libspage.communityEmpty: No libraries published by others yet. One appears when someone publishes a cortex with a library file and a guide on the Extensions page and makes it public.
libspage.hint.base: The in-the-app column is the name the code calls the library by, and under it how many published apps load it. Base libraries have no version number: they follow this server and promise not to break their API.
libspage.hint.ui: A library by others is a cortex anyone published with a library file and a guide; it sits in this list as a row like the platform's own, and its guide comes from the cortex's own prompt. The same cortex is on the Extensions page from its owner's side: managed there, taken into use here.
libspage.hint.third: The version is in the file name (phaser@3.min.js, phaser@4.min.js), so an old app never breaks when a new version arrives. A deprecated library stays served and its row says what replaces it. Licence, size and source are in the opened row.
libspage.copiedToast: The lines and the guide of {id} are copied for an AI.
libspage.intoAppOne: One line in the app's head.
libspage.forAiBody: The guide, {n} characters: what the library does, how it is called and what differs from what a model remembers.
libspage.forAiNone: This library has no separate guide; the lines and the API are enough.
libspage.forAiSub: An AI fetches the same guide itself at /v1/library-packs/{id}.
libspage.provenNone: No run on any model yet. The row still says which model it suits, because that is known from the version.
libspage.provenSub: A run is added with its evidence: the model, the result, what it cost and where to see it. Without evidence it is not claimed.
libspage.usedBySub: Read from the published apps' source when they were published.
libspage.usedNoneSub: The map is read from published apps' source; a draft or someone else's private app does not show.
libspage.seeWorkingSub: The same library at work; the demo template is in the Create menu of the Apps launcher.
libspage.versionSub: A major version is always a new file: the next one arrives beside this one, never in its place.
libspage.noVersionSub: A base library follows this server and promises not to break its API.
libspage.deprecatedWith: Stays served, but a new app takes {id} instead.
libspage.deprecatedWithout: Stays served; no replacement is named.
libspage.aiIntro: The app build guide lists these libraries already, so most of the time you do nothing: the AI picks a library from the idea and reads its guide. This page is for seeing what exists, what someone already uses and what is proven to work.
libspage.ruleLabel: The rule an AI takes with it
libspage.ruleBody: Before a library is used, the AI fetches its guide at {base}/v1/library-packs/<id> and reads the fields ai_doc and changelog. The whole index is at {base}/v1/library-packs. A library is always loaded from here, never from an outside CDN, and a major version is always a new file: when chartjs@5.js appears, chartjs@4.js stays where it is, so an app that keeps its lines keeps working.
libspage.aiModelBody: Third-party libraries say which model they suit. For every model: the version is the one models remember anyway. For a strong model: the version differs from what models remember, and a weak model writes the old API unless it reads the guide; the row carries that one warning. The platform's own libraries have nothing to remember, so an AI reads the guide first.
libspage.aiModelSub: The words come from the registry: any, frontier, needs-doc. They do not show on the page.
libspage.aiProvenBody: {n} libraries have been run through the same task list on a model and checked in a browser: {runs} runs, {passed} passed and {failed} crashed. The row says the model, the result and what the run cost. A run is added by a developer or an agent with its evidence; the page does not let it be claimed without.
libspage.aiProvenSub: A run on a library by others is the author's own report, and is marked as such.
libspage.aiUsedBody: The same dependency map as on the Extensions page: the published apps' source says which libraries they load. {using} apps of {total} use one of these, and {unused} libraries are not in any app yet.
libspage.aiUsedBodyShort: The same dependency map as on the Extensions page: the published apps' source says which libraries they load. {libs} libraries are in use, and {unused} are not in any app yet.
capspage.titleSub: what an agent can find here by name, and call
capspage.desc: Every extension action, app tool and agent offer here, in the one registry an agent searches by word. The agent reads the id, the input shape and the price, then calls or commissions. Cortexes are browser libraries an app loads, so they live on the Libraries page.
capspage.descEmpty: Nothing here is yours yet. Activate an extension, publish an app tool or list an agent offer, and it appears here on its own within a minute.
capspage.copyRule: Copy the rule for your AI
capspage.ruleCopiedToast: The rule is on your clipboard. Paste it into your AI's instructions.
capspage.stripToolsNone: no app publishes a tool manifest yet
capspage.stripOffersNone: no agent lists a public offer yet
capspage.stripOtherOn: adding by hand is open here
capspage.stripOtherOff: adding by hand is closed here
capspage.secAi: How an agent finds and calls
capspage.emptyExt: No extension is active here yet. An active extension's actions appear here on their own.
capspage.emptyApp: No app here publishes a tool manifest yet. When one does, its tools appear here with their price.
capspage.emptyAgent: No agent here lists a public offer yet. An offer listed on the Offers page appears here.
capspage.emptyOther: Nothing has been added by hand.
capspage.search.ext: Search by extension, action or what it does
capspage.search.app: Search by app, tool or what it does
capspage.search.agent: Search by agent, offer or what it does
capspage.hint.ext: An action runs inside the extension's sandbox on this server. The agent calls it by id, and the call is proxied through the registry so it counts.
capspage.hint.app: An app tool is a contract, not a direct call: the agent accepts the offer, pays the price in morsels, and then invokes the tool.
capspage.hint.agent: An agent offer is work another agent does on request. The agent accepts it and hands over the task; delivery arrives as a work item.
capspage.manualBody: A capability you write yourself: a name, a summary and, if you want it callable, a webhook the registry forwards the call to. Use it for a service that lives outside this server and has no extension.
capspage.manualOn: Adding is open here. The form is below.
capspage.manualOff: Adding is closed here: the publishing policy is {policy}. The operator sets it.
capspage.policyBody: Publishing by hand: {publishing}. Who may publish: {publishers}. Webhooks: {webhooks}.
capspage.policySub: Three settings the operator makes for the whole server. They govern hand-added entries only; extensions, apps and agents register on their own.
capspage.policy.self_only: for your own use only, not listed to others
capspage.policy.moderated: open, the operator reviews each one
capspage.publishers.allowlist: people on the operator's list only
capspage.webhooks.disabled: closed, so a hand-added entry is discovery only
capspage.webhooks.allowlist_only: addresses on the operator's list only
capspage.formSummary: What it does, in one or two sentences
capspage.formHint: Without a webhook the entry is discovery only. With one, the registry forwards each call to that address.
capspage.aiIntro: The registry is one list an agent searches by word. Each entry says what the thing does, what it takes, what it returns, what it costs and who may call it. The agent then calls by id, or accepts a contract when the entry is an app tool or an agent offer.
capspage.ruleBody: Find first, read one, then call: list the registry by word, read the entry's input and output shape, then invoke by id. Without MCP the same three are GET and POST on {base}/v1/capabilities. Copy the rule below into your AI's instructions and it does this on its own.
capspage.aiWhoBody: Each entry says whether a call needs no sign-in, any signed-in principal, or a registered agent. A priced entry is paid in morsels when the contract is accepted, and the price is in the entry.
capspage.aiTrustBody: A vouch is a person saying this capability did what it says. Vouch for others' entries you have used; you cannot vouch for your own. The operator's review is a separate mark.
capspage.aiTrustSub: {n} vouches on this server so far.
capspage.aiTrustNone: No vouches on this server yet.
capspage.aiCallsOn: {n} calls counted so far. Counting is on here: every extension action call counts, whichever door it came through.
capspage.aiCallsOff: {n} calls counted so far. Only calls that go through the registry count here; a direct extension call is not counted. The operator can turn full counting on.
capspage.aiTwoBody: This registry is what people and their agents have provided here. The server's own tools (memory, apps, organisms, messages) are a separate catalogue the agent reaches with its discover tool.
capspage.discoveryOnlySub: This entry is found here and used through its contract door, which the usage line above names.
capspage.tryHint: A real call through the registry, counted like any other. Edit the input first.
capspage.tryBadJson: The input is not valid JSON.
capspage.forAgentSub: The agent reads {id} first, then calls with the input the entry names.
capspage.whoMayCallSub: Set by the provider. A priced call is paid when the contract is accepted.
capspage.trustSub: A vouch is a person saying this did what it says.
capspage.callsCounted: Every call counts here, whichever door it came through.
capspage.callsProxyOnly: Only calls through the registry count here. Direct extension calls are not counted unless the operator turns counting on.
capspage.sourceSub.ext: Activate, deactivate or remove the extension there; the actions here follow within a minute.
capspage.sourceSub.app: The tool manifest is published with the app; the entries here follow it.
capspage.sourceSub.agent: The offer is listed on the Offers page; the entries here follow it.
capspage.webhookNone: none, so this is discovery only
capspage.webhookSub: The address the registry forwards each call to.
capspage.copyFailed: Copying failed. Select the text and copy it yourself.
capspage.copiedToast: {name} is on your clipboard, ready for your agent.
capspage.unvouchedToast: Your vouch for {name} is taken back.
capspage.confirmRemove: Remove {name}? Agents stop finding it at once.
skpage.titleSub: what your agent knows how to do here, by reference and not by copy
skpage.desc: A skill is a SKILL.md pack: a guide that tells an agent how something is done here, the right way. The agent loads it by reference, never as a copy, so a fix shows everywhere at once. Your own skills come first, then this server's library and the skills of your workspaces.
skpage.descEmpty: You have no skill of your own yet, but your agent already knows {n} things from this server's library. A skill of your own is worth writing the second time you find yourself explaining the same thing to your AI.
skpage.copyRule: Copy the rule for your AI
skpage.ruleCopiedToast: The rule is on your clipboard. Paste it into your AI's instructions.
skpage.stripOwnSub: {bound} bound to an app · {mine} only for you
skpage.stripWsNone: you are not yet in a workspace that has any
skpage.secAi: How an agent loads a skill
skpage.emptyOwn: No skill of your own yet.
skpage.emptyOwnSub: The fastest first one is to ask your AI to write it: the request is ready below. If you are building an app, bind the skill to it, and every agent that runs the app gets it on its own.
skpage.emptyWs: None of your workspaces has a skill yet. A skill published in a workspace shows here.
skpage.search.own: Search by name, app or content
skpage.hint.own: A skill only for you is seen by you and your agents, one for members by everyone signed in here, and a public one outside this server as well. Section 05 says when a skill loads.
skpage.hint.node: Library skills can be fetched by every agent on this server. Some came with the server as guides, and the operator may edit them; the rest were published here. You cannot edit these, but you can copy the ref, download the pack or attach a skill to your agent.
skpage.hint.ws: A workspace skill can be read by every member and member agent, and it travels with the workspace's export and template. It is edited on the workspace's own Skills tab.
skpage.who.appSub: every agent that runs the app
skpage.who.appAndAgents: every agent that runs the app · attached to {n}
skpage.who.noAgents: No agent has attached this yet.
skpage.who.allSub: everyone signed in here may load it
skpage.who.allLong: Every agent on this server may load it.
skpage.who.builtin: a guide that came with the server
skpage.who.wsLong: Every member and member agent of the workspace may load it.
skpage.who.freeSub: loads when an agent fetches it by name
skpage.who.freeOwner: you and your agents, when fetched by name
skpage.who.freeLong: Not bound to an app. It loads when an agent fetches it by name, or when you attach it to an agent.
skpage.who.attachSub: Attaching a skill to an agent makes it load fresh every time that agent starts.
skpage.refSub: Copy either one for your agent. The version-locked ref always gives this text; the unlocked one gives the newest.
skpage.versionSub: Publishing the same name again raises the version number; the newest ten stay retrievable by a locked ref.
skpage.vis.membersSub: Everyone signed in on this server.
skpage.vis.workspaceSub: Every member and member agent of the workspace.
skpage.vis.change: changes at once, without a new version
skpage.installSub: Into Claude Code or Claude Desktop. For claude.ai, download the zip and drop it under Skills. A connected AI needs no install.
skpage.newIntro: Two roads. The first is what this server exists for: ask your AI to write the skill and publish it. The second is to write it yourself in the editor.
skpage.roadAskBody: Copy this into your conversation and replace the bracketed parts with your own. The AI writes the skill, checks it and publishes it into your skills; if it binds it to an app, every agent that runs the app gets it at once.
skpage.roadWriteBody: In the header a name (lowercase, words joined with hyphens) and a description that says what the skill does and when to use it. Below it, the expertise itself. Publishing the same name again raises the version number.
skpage.editorPlaceholder:
---
name: my-skill
description: what it does, and when to use it
---

The expertise…
skpage.editorHint: Publish it only for you first, and open it to others later when it is ready.
skpage.aiIntro: A skill is always loaded by reference, never by copying. The ref says where the skill lives and whose it is: in the server's library, among an owner's own, or in a workspace. A version can be locked on the end, @1.0.4, so the agent gets exactly that text and not the newest. The ref forms are in the rule below.
skpage.ruleBody: Before running an app, list its bound skills and read them. When you do not know how something is done here, search for a skill by name before guessing. When the owner attaches a skill to you, load it fresh every time. Copy the rule below into your AI's instructions and it does this on its own.
skpage.aiWhoBody: A skill bound to an app loads for every agent that runs that app. A skill attached to an agent loads for that agent every time. A free skill loads when an agent fetches it.
skpage.aiWhoSub: Attach from the agent's own page, from a skill's opened row here, or by asking your AI.
skpage.aiVisBody: Only for you: you and your agents. For members: everyone signed in on this server. Public: readable from elsewhere too, and listed in the public index.
skpage.aiVisSub: {n} public skills are now at {url}, where any AI finds them without signing in.
skpage.aiVersionsBody: Publishing the same name again raises the version number, and the newest ten stay retained. Lock a version when the agent's work must not change under it; leave it unlocked when you want fixes to show at once.
skpage.aiInstallBody: A skill works as it is in Claude Code, Claude Desktop and claude.ai: run the line below, or download the .zip and drop it into claude.ai's skills. A connected AI needs no install; it loads the skill when it needs it.
skpage.zipToast: The zip is downloaded. Upload it under Skills in claude.ai, or unzip it into ~/.claude/skills.
skpage.confirmRemove: Remove {name}? An agent that holds its ref will report it as unresolved.
pkpage.titleSub: ready-made wholes that install as your own
pkpage.desc: A package is a whole that installs in one go: an app, its server extension and browser library, memory defaults and translations. Installing makes you your own copy of every part, and the copies are yours to edit from then on. A new package comes from asking your AI to build one.
pkpage.descEmpty: You have not installed a package yet. {n} are on offer, and each installs in one go as your own. Your own package comes from asking your AI to build one.
pkpage.copyRequest: Copy the request for your AI
pkpage.copyFailed: Copying failed. Select the text and copy it yourself.
pkpage.promptCopiedToast: The package builder's request is on your clipboard. Paste it into your AI and say what you want built.
pkpage.promptFailed: The request could not be fetched from this server.
pkpage.stripInstalledNone: pick one below and give it a name
pkpage.stripOffersSub: {system} came with the server · {others} by others
pkpage.stripOwnNone: ask your AI, or import a .zip
pkpage.stripRemoteNone: the federation has brought none yet
pkpage.emptyInstalledSub: When you install one from below, its parts appear here as your own copies, and this row says what was made and where to open it.
pkpage.emptyOffers: Nothing is on offer here yet.
pkpage.emptyOwn: You have not published a package. Ask your AI to build one, or import a .zip.
pkpage.hintInstalled: An installed package is a set of parts in your name: the app on the Apps page, the extension and the browser library on the Extensions page, the defaults and translations in Memory. Open the row to see every part's name; the update check says whether the package has a newer version.
pkpage.hintOffers: Install makes you your own copy of every part and asks for a name on this row, not in a separate window. The packages that came with the server are examples the operator keeps current; the ones others published are as they are.
pkpage.hintOwn: A public package is on offer to everyone on this server. One proposed to the gallery goes to the operator's review, and an approved one shows on other servers too. A new version is published under the same name; installed copies stay as they are until their owner checks for the update.
pkpage.syncedToast: The listings from other servers are fetched.
pkpage.partsLabel: Parts · each is your own copy
pkpage.packageGone: the package is no longer on offer
pkpage.updateNone: The package has no newer version.
pkpage.updateSub: An update replaces the app, the extension and the browser library and leaves memory and translations alone. An edited part is asked about first.
pkpage.confirmUpdate: Update to {version}? The app, the extension and the browser library are replaced; memory and translations stay as they are.
pkpage.forAgentInstance: There is no separate tool for an installed package: an agent sees the parts on their own lists, the app among the apps and the extension among the extensions.
pkpage.forAgentInstanceSub: Copy the parts' registered names when you want to point at one.
pkpage.confirmRemove: Remove {name} and its {n} parts? The app, the extension, the browser library and the stored defaults are deleted.
pkpage.labelPlaceholder: A name for your copy, for example the company's name
pkpage.installSub: Installing takes a moment and then says what was made. Every part is yours afterwards.
pkpage.installOwnSub: You can install your own package as many times as you like; each copy gets its own name.
pkpage.installedToast: {name} is installed: {n} parts in your name.
pkpage.makerSystem: An example that came with the server, kept current by the operator.
pkpage.makerRemote: From the server {node}, through the federation.
pkpage.vis.privateLong: Private: only you can install it.
pkpage.vis.publicLong: Public: on offer to everyone on this server.
pkpage.proposedToast: {name} is proposed to the gallery; the operator will review it.
pkpage.madePublicToast: {name} is now on offer to everyone here.
pkpage.versionsSub: A new version is published under the same name. Installed copies stay as they are until their owner checks for the update.
pkpage.confirmArchive: Remove the package {name} and all its versions? Installed copies keep working, but nobody can install it again.
pkpage.newIntro: Two roads. The first is what this server exists for: ask your AI to build the package and publish it. The second is to import a ready .zip.
pkpage.roadAsk: Ask your AI to build one
pkpage.roadAskBody: Copy the request into your conversation. It carries the package builder's whole guide: the AI asks what you want, chooses the parts, builds them, tests them and publishes the package into your publications, or hands you a .zip to import.
pkpage.roadAskSub: The same guide this server has always carried; nothing to install.
pkpage.roadZipBody: A finished package comes as a .zip with its manifest and parts inside. The import checks the file and publishes the package as private among your publications, from where you can install it and make it public.
pkpage.aiIntro: A package is a set of installable parts, not an app: apps have their own page, and an agent finds them with a different tool. An agent lists the packages, reads the one you mean and installs it under the name you give; installing registers every part in your name.
pkpage.ruleBody: The rule tells your agent this: when the owner asks to set up something that is on offer as a package (a company brain, a shop), list the packages, read the description and the parts, and install under the name the owner gives. Ask for the name before installing. An app is not a package. Copy the rule below into your AI's instructions and it does this on its own.
pkpage.aiInstallBody: Every part becomes your own copy in your name: the app is published, the extension and the browser library are installed and switched on, the memory defaults and translations are written. Parts get unique names, so the same package can be installed twice.
pkpage.aiInstallSub: The copy is yours: an edited part is marked, and an update does not replace it without asking.
pkpage.aiUpdateBody: A new version of a package does not change an installed copy. The update check says whether a newer version is out, and the update replaces the app, the extension and the browser library while leaving memory and translations alone.
pkpage.aiPublishBody: Your AI publishes a package directly (aimeat_package_publish) or hands you a .zip. A private package is yours alone to install; a public one is on offer here; one proposed to the gallery goes to the operator's review.
pfpage.desc: Your page is one HTML document at your address: who you are, what you do here and how to reach you. For a newcomer it begins as the welcome mat, an introduction page an AI writes from one request. You change it by asking your AI, with the builder from your own content, or by bringing a finished HTML file, and every publish replaces the previous page completely.
pfpage.descOff: Your page was taken off the web on {date}. It has not been deleted: the page is stored exactly as it was published, and one press puts it back at its addresses. Until then a visitor at your addresses is told there is no page, and you are not in the member showcase.
pfpage.descNone: You have no page at your address yet. The first version is your welcome mat: an introduction page your AI writes from one request and you paste into your front page (Home). Once it is there, the page appears here with its addresses and switches.
pfpage.askAi: Ask your AI to improve the page
pfpage.stripSearchOn: and search engines may list it
pfpage.stripSearchOff: shared by link, not in search engines
pfpage.addressNodeSub: Always works. The member showcase, search engines and your AI use this address.
pfpage.addressOwnSub: The same page on its own subdomain, without the frame of this site.
pfpage.badgeOn: A small AIMEAT mark sits at the foot of the page.
pfpage.hintAddresses: Both addresses show the same page. The own address is the one you hand to people; the server address is the one the member showcase and search engines point at.
pfpage.hintAddressOne: This server serves pages at one address; an own subdomain per person is something the operator can turn on.
pfpage.visWebOnSub: Anyone with the address sees your page.
pfpage.visWebOffSub: A visitor at your addresses is told there is no page, until you publish it again.
pfpage.visWebHint: Taking it off the web deletes nothing: the page stays stored as it is, and one press puts it back.
pfpage.visSearchOnSub: Search engines may list your page; showing up usually takes a few days.
pfpage.visSearchOffSub: The page works and can be shared by link, and search engines are told to leave it out.
pfpage.visSearchOffWebAllowed: because the page is off the web. Your choice (allowed) waits for the publish.
pfpage.visSearchOffWebDenied: because the page is off the web, and your choice (not allowed) stays.
pfpage.visSearchHint: A switch of its own, because the page carries your name: a page shared by link does not have to show up in search engines.
pfpage.searchOff: Take it out of search engines
pfpage.visShowcaseOnSub: You appear in this server's member showcase, the list of people who made a page, with {n} more.
pfpage.visShowcaseOffSub: The showcase lists only pages that are on the web, and yours was taken off.
pfpage.visShowcaseHint: This one is not set on its own: it follows the On the web switch.
pfpage.previewHint: The preview shows the page exactly as a visitor sees it, and the page cannot reach your own data.
pfpage.writerMat: Written as your welcome mat by {who}.
pfpage.writerMatUnknown: Written as your welcome mat; the page did not say which AI wrote it.
pfpage.writerMatSub: A page born from the welcome mat names the model and the app it was written with.
pfpage.writerUnknown: Not known: the page was published without saying who wrote it.
pfpage.writerUnknownSub: A page born from the welcome mat names the model and the app it was written with, for example "Claude Opus · Claude Desktop".
pfpage.choicesSub: Choices made in the builder. They go along when you ask for the next version; the published page is already written and does not change from them.
pfpage.sizeSub: One HTML file with everything the page needs. Images and memory records it fetches by their addresses from this server.
pfpage.storageIn: Stored as a file under your name:
pfpage.storageSub: Every publish replaces it completely. Taking the page off the web does not touch the file.
pfpage.changeIntro: Three ways to the same result. The first is what this server is for: your AI reads the page and publishes a new one. The second writes a request from your own content for any AI. The third takes a finished page in.
pfpage.roadAiBody: Tell your AI what the page needs: "improve my page", "add my latest project", "write it in Finnish". It reads the current page, writes a new one and publishes it at this address. Look at the result at your address.
pfpage.roadAiBodyNew: If your AI is already connected to this server, tell it: "make me a page for AIMEAT". It writes the page and publishes it straight to your address.
pfpage.roadBuilderBody: Choose from your own content what goes on the page (images, boards, browser libraries, memory records), a style and a purpose. The builder writes a request you run in any AI, and the answer is pasted into the field next to it.
pfpage.roadBuilderBodyNew: Choose from your own content what goes on the page, and a style. The builder writes a request for any AI and takes the answer in to publish.
pfpage.roadImportBody: Paste a finished page here or choose a file. Publishing replaces the current page; the limit is {max} kB.
pfpage.pasteSize: {n} kB · fits the limit of {max} kB
pfpage.pasteTooBig: {n} kB · over the limit of {max} kB
pfpage.pasteNotWhole: That is not a whole HTML document: it needs <html> and </html>.
pfpage.emptyNoneSub: Your address is reserved for you; a visitor there is told there is no page until the first one is published.
pfpage.roadMatBody: The first step of your home is this introduction page. Copy the request for your AI and paste its answer into the field on your front page (Home): it reads from the answer which AI you have, and publishes the page at your address.
pfpage.aiIntro: Your page is within your AI's reach: it reads the same page you see, writes it anew as a whole and publishes it. Publishing replaces the previous page, so a change always begins with reading.
pfpage.ruleBody: When the person you act for asks to change their page or portfolio, read the current page first, make the requested change to the whole page and publish it. Tell them the address and ask them to look. A company's page is a different thing and a different tool.
pfpage.aiDoesBody: Rewrites the page's file and leaves the switches as they are: a page on the web stays on the web, and the search-engine permission does not change.
pfpage.aiDoesSub: Limit {max} kB. A larger page is refused, and your AI is told why in plain words.
pfpage.aiNotBody: It does not take the page off the web and does not change the search-engine permission; those are your switches on this page.
pfpage.aiNotSub: Your AI needs permission to store files (storage:write); you grant it on the Agents page.
pfpage.aiAddressBody: The publish answer names both addresses, this server's and your own, so your AI can hand you a link that opens.
pfpage.aiAddressBodyNew: The publish answer names the address the page opens at, so your AI can hand you a link that opens.
pfpage.confirmUnpublish: Take your page off the web? Nothing is deleted: the page stays stored here, and you can make it public again from this page whenever you like.
pfpage.unpublishedToast: Taken off the web. The page is still stored here.
pfpage.searchOnToast: Search engines may find your page. Showing up usually takes a few days.
pfpage.badgeOnToast: The AIMEAT mark shows at the foot of your own address.
pfpage.badgeOffToast: The AIMEAT mark is hidden on your own address.
pfpage.copiedRequest: The request is on the clipboard. Paste it into your AI's chat.
pfpage.copiedRule: The rule is on the clipboard.
pfpage.copiedMat: The welcome-mat request is on the clipboard. Paste it into your AI's chat, and its answer into the field on your home.
pfpage.publishedToast: Published: {n} kB. Look at your address.
aipage.desc: The AI features here run on your own key: what apps ask, what agents do, voice messages turned into text and attached images read. On this page you choose which model answers what, and how much may be spent in a day. The built-in chat is the exception: {host} pays for it on its own key.
aipage.descNoKey: You have no key of your own, so the AI features run on {host}'s key for as long as the starter allowance lasts; {n} is left. With your own key everything runs on your own budget and the model you choose, with no allowance to run out. An ordinary answer costs a fraction of a cent. Put $10 on OpenRouter once and its free models rise to a thousand requests a day.
aipage.providerChoice.lmstudio: LM Studio on your own machine
aipage.providerHint: OpenRouter relays hundreds of models from dozens of makers through one key. A local or own server needs no key, but reports no prices.
aipage.keyMasked: stored, encrypted; a new key replaces the old one
aipage.keyHint: The key is stored encrypted on this server and never shown again after saving. Get it from OpenRouter's Keys page; the same account shows your balance and bill.
aipage.keyStoredHint: The test makes a real request and says which model answered and how long it took. If the request fails, the test says which it was: the key is wrong, or the daily budget is spent.
aipage.noKeyBody: The chat works on {host}'s key and model. Apps and agents get AI on {host}'s key until the starter allowance is spent; then they say an own key is needed.
aipage.roleWhat.chat: Answers everything that has no model of its own: apps' AI requests, agents' scheduled work, the notebook.
aipage.roleWhat.reasoning: Demanding planning and analysis in workflows and calibration. Pick a slower, more careful model here if your workflows make decisions.
aipage.roleWhat.execution: Writing code and tests. A cheaper, fast model is usually enough.
aipage.roleWhat.vision: Reads the images you attach to a message or send to the secretary, your AI assistant here. If your default model reads images itself, this can stay empty.
aipage.roleWhat.stt: Turns voice messages into text. Without a model, voice messages stay untranscribed.
aipage.roleWhat.image: Makes an image on request. Without a model an image request cannot succeed, and the asker is told so plainly.
aipage.roleOff: off until a model is chosen
aipage.roleImageOff: this server's default, if the operator set one
aipage.roleLeadUnsetDefault: Nothing chosen: the default model answers.
aipage.searchModels: Search {n} models by name or id…
aipage.recommended: Recommended · kept up from the catalogue by itself
aipage.poolFacts.transcription: {n} models that turn speech into text
aipage.sttNone: This provider offers no speech models.
aipage.imageNone: This provider offers no image-making models.
aipage.modelsNone: No models to choose from yet. Save the key, then refresh the list.
aipage.sttLanguageHint: A hint helps with one known language; leave it detecting for mixed speech.
aipage.sttMeasuredBody: Record a few seconds and the page turns them into text for real and tells you the price.
aipage.sttMeasuredSub: A speech model's listed price has no unit (the same number is per minute at one provider and per hour at another), so one measured request says more than the list. Recording up to {max} seconds; a voice message on this server may be {limit} seconds.
aipage.hintUnits: Prices are per million tokens: a token is about half a word, and an ordinary answer is a few hundred tokens, a fraction of a cent. "In" is what you send the model, "out" is what it answers. Context is how much text the model keeps in mind at once; 1 000 k is about a novel.
aipage.hintModels: Change opens the search on the same row: the recommended first (the free router that picks a model for you, the cheapest that reads images, the cheapest with a large context), then the whole list with prices. A choice is stored on the row at once. A role without a model uses the default model; speech and image making are the exception, and without a model they are off.
aipage.hintModelsNoKey: Models are chosen once a key is stored: the list is fetched from the provider with your key.
aipage.dailyBudgetBody: {n} a day, {today} spent today. Once the budget is spent, further requests are refused and the asker is told why.
aipage.dailyBudgetSub: This server's default is {def}. An ordinary answer costs a fraction of a cent; your last 30 days cost {month}, about {perDay} a day.
aipage.monthBody: {cost} · requests {calls} · tokens {tokens} · apps {apps}, of which {big} spent at least 10 cents.
aipage.monthNone: Nothing spent in the last 30 days.
aipage.monthSub: The cost is what the provider reported; the binding bill is in your provider's own view.
aipage.capsHint: ordered by 30-day cost · limit = at most this much a day for that app
aipage.capsEditingHint: write the limit on the row · empty = no limit
aipage.hintCaps: Every app may use the whole daily budget unless it has a limit of its own. The limit is written on the row.
aipage.noSpend: No app has spent anything in the last 30 days.
aipage.chartTitle: Spend by day · {n} most recent days with spending ({first} to {last})
aipage.paramsIntro: These apply to every request that does not say otherwise. For most people the defaults are enough.
aipage.tempSub: 0 = the same answer to the same question, 1 = the model's own default, 2 = the freest.
aipage.topPSub: How wide a vocabulary the model picks from: 0.1 narrow, 1.0 the whole range.
aipage.maxTokensSub: In tokens; a long limit costs nothing if the answer is short.
aipage.retryOn: Retry when the answer is not in the requested form
aipage.retryBody: On, at most {n} times, when the answer is not in the requested form (broken JSON, for example).
aipage.retryOff: Off: a malformed answer is returned as it came.
aipage.retrySub: Concerns apps and workflows that ask for structured answers.
aipage.consumersIntro: Everything here that asks the AI in your name spends your key. Every request is recorded under the app's name, and every one draws on the same daily budget.
aipage.consumerAppsBody: An app asks the AI under its own name (AIMEAT.ai.complete).
aipage.consumerAppsTop: The biggest in the last 30 days: {apps}.
aipage.consumerAgentsBody: Scheduled jobs and workflows are recorded under the job's name (schedule:…, workflow:…).
aipage.consumerMediaBody: A voice message costs by its length, an attached image by the image model's price. Both from the same daily budget.
aipage.consumerChatNode: Does not spend your key: {host} pays for it on its own key and model ({model}).
aipage.consumerChatOwn: Runs on your own key and your default model.
aipage.consumerChatAllowance: Runs on this server's key while your allowance lasts ({n} left).
aipage.consumerChatUnknown: The chat's payer could not be read right now.
aipage.consumerChatSub: If the chat later moves to run through this server, it starts using your key and the models you chose.
aipage.consumerAgentRuleBody: An agent does not change these: the key, the models and the budget are yours. It sees whether AI is available, and gets a plain reason when the budget is spent.
aipage.modelsEmpty: The provider returned no models. Check the address.
aipage.modelsError: Could not load the models. Check the address and the key, save, then refresh.
aipage.testBudgetSpent: The daily budget is spent; the key itself is fine
aipage.confirmRemove: Remove your API key and AI settings from this server? Apps and agents lose AI until a key is stored again.
aipage.budgetRange: The budget must be a number between 0 and 1000.
aipage.capRange: The limit for "{app}" must be a number between 0 and 1000.
calpage.listDesc: You give one prompt and an example of the answer you want (the target output). A calibration runs the prompt on several models, and one model as the judge compares each answer with your example point by point, scores it and proposes corrections to the prompt. From the corrections you choose, the next version of the prompt is written. Every run is kept, so you can see whether the prompt got better.
calpage.newPlaceholder: Name of the new calibration, e.g. Weekly report prompt
calpage.emptyBody: Name one above. Then write the prompt and the target output, choose the models, and start the first run.
calpage.stateNoPrompt: No prompt yet. Next: write the prompt and the target output.
calpage.listHint: The score is the weighted share of checkpoints that passed in the latest run: a critical checkpoint counts 3, a major one 2, a minor one 1.
calpage.projectDesc: Result first: the latest run and what did not pass, then the prompt and the target output with their versions, the models, and the four instruction prompts the calibrator speaks to the models with.
calpage.projectDescTrend: This calibration went from {from} % to {to} % in {n} runs.
calpage.needKey: A run needs your own AI key. Add it on the AI page.
calpage.needPrompt: A run needs a saved prompt. Write it in 02.
calpage.needCandidate: A run needs at least one model under test. Add one in 03.
calpage.archivedMsg: Archived. It stays readable behind the archived door on the list.
calpage.confirmDeleteCalibration: Delete the calibration "{name}" with all its versions and runs? This cannot be undone.
calpage.noRunsBody: When the prompt, the target output and at least one model are in place, "New run" above runs all four steps and the result lands here.
calpage.hintRuns: A run takes four steps: every model under test answers the prompt; the judge compares each answer with the target output checkpoint by checkpoint; the judge and the models themselves propose corrections to the prompt; and a summary groups the proposals into three options. The percentage is the weighted share of checkpoints that passed: a critical checkpoint counts 3, a major one 2, a minor one 1. Open a run to see the steps, the checkpoints and the proposals; the next version of the prompt is made from there.
calpage.chartTitle: Score per model over the runs
calpage.emptyRunsWhat: These carry no answer, no score and no proposal. They can go.
calpage.confirmDeleteEmpties: Delete the empty runs ({n})? Nothing is lost: none of them ever ran a step.
calpage.runLead: Run {n} was made with version {v} on {date} at {time}.
calpage.runLeadTook: It took {d}, as long as the slowest model.
calpage.runLeadOptions: The summary offers three options for the next version, in step 4 below.
calpage.confirmDeleteRun: Delete this run with its answers, scores and proposals?
calpage.stepWhat.generate: Every model under test answers the prompt as it is. The answer is kept in full, with the time it took.
calpage.stepWhat.analyze: The judge compares each answer with the target output checkpoint by checkpoint: structure, not wording. Each checkpoint passes or fails and weighs critical 3, major 2 or minor 1; the score is the passed share.
calpage.stepWhat.reflect: Two lists per model: the judge's proposals for changing the prompt, and the model's own, from what it got wrong itself.
calpage.stepWhat.synthesize: The judge groups every proposal, marks impact and risk, and packs them into three options: A conservative, B moderate, C all of them. Choose one and the next version of the prompt is written from it.
calpage.copyStepPrompts: Copy a prompt to your own AI:
calpage.stepNeedsPrevious: This step needs the previous one first.
calpage.noOutputsYet: No answers yet: run step 1 first.
calpage.noScoresYet: No scores yet: run step 2 first.
calpage.noSynthesisYet: No summary yet: run step 4, or paste one.
calpage.applyHint: The judge rewrites the prompt with the chosen proposals and saves it as the next version. The old versions stay.
calpage.applyingHint: This takes a minute or two. Keep the page open.
calpage.copyApplyPrompt: Copy the rewrite prompt for your own AI
calpage.pasteLabel.analyze: The judge's comparison, as it answered
calpage.pasteLabel.reflect: The proposals, as they were answered
calpage.pasteLabel.synthesize: The summary, as it was answered
calpage.pastePlaceholder: Paste the answer here, exactly as your AI gave it.
calpage.progress.analyze: Step 2: the judge is scoring the answers ({n})…
calpage.progress.synthesize: Step 4: the judge is grouping the proposals…
calpage.errProvider: The AI provider did not answer.
calpage.errEmpty: The model {model} returned an empty answer. Try again.
calpage.errTimeout: The call took over thirty minutes and was stopped.
calpage.errNoCandidate: This model is no longer among the models under test.
calpage.errNoProposals: The chosen option has no proposals.
calpage.errNoPrompt: The run's prompt version could not be read.
calpage.errApplyShort: The judge returned too short a text to be a prompt. Try again, or with a stronger judge.
calpage.noVersionBody: Write the prompt on the left and, on the right, an example of the answer you want. Saving makes version 1.
calpage.viewingOld: You are reading version {n}. It cannot be edited; the current version can.
calpage.promptPlaceholder: The prompt you want to calibrate, word for word as the model gets it.
calpage.targetPlaceholder: An example of the answer you want. The judge compares its structure, not its wording.
calpage.saveVersionHint: Saving never overwrites: every version stays, and the runs remember which one they used.
calpage.saveFirstVersionHint: The first version unlocks the first run.
calpage.hintPrompt: Change the prompt here between runs, or let a run's summary write the next version for you.
calpage.noKeyBody: The models are picked from your provider's catalogue on the AI page, and a run uses your key.
calpage.judgeFromAiReasoning: the reasoning model from your AI page
calpage.judgeFromAiDefault: your default model from the AI page (no reasoning model chosen)
calpage.judgeFromServer: no model chosen on the AI page
calpage.judgeLeadOwn: This calibration uses {name} as its judge. Pick another below, or go back to the AI page's choice.
calpage.judgeLeadAi: The judge is {name}, from your AI page. Pick a model here only if this calibration needs a different one.
calpage.judgeCleared: The judge follows the AI page again.
calpage.noCandidatesHint: No models under test yet; a run needs at least one.
calpage.hintModels: The judge should be a strong model: it reads every answer and writes the proposals. The models under test are the ones you want the prompt to work on.
calpage.modelsNone: The catalogue is empty. Refresh it on the AI page.
calpage.templatesIntro: These are the texts the calibrator speaks to the models with. The defaults serve most calibrations; open one to read it, change it, or put the default back.
calpage.tplWhat.analysis: Tells the judge to compare structure, not wording; at most eight checkpoints, each critical, major or minor; the answer in a fixed form.
calpage.tplWhat.reflection: Asks the judge for general corrections to the prompt, no project names: what to add and where.
calpage.tplWhat.selfReflection: Asks the model that answered what in the prompt misled it, and what would have guided it better.
calpage.tplWhat.synthesis: Asks the judge to group the proposals, mark impact and risk, and build the options A, B and C.
calpage.tplSlots.analysis: Filled in at run time: the target output, the model's answer, the model's name and the prompt.
calpage.tplSlots.reflection: Filled in at run time: the prompt, the target output, the model's answer, the model's name and the judge's comparison.
calpage.tplSlots.selfReflection: Filled in at run time: the prompt, the target output, the model's answer, the model's name and the judge's comparison.
calpage.tplSlots.synthesis: Filled in at run time: the prompt, the judge's proposals and the models' own proposals.
calpage.roadsIntro: A calibration runs two ways. On this page a run is made on your key with one press. Without a key, every step can be copied to your own AI and the answer pasted back: the run goes the same way, through your hands.
calpage.roadLeadBody: Say to your AI: "calibrate my prompt {name} and make the next version from the moderate option". It reads the prompt and the target output, runs the steps on its own model and brings the answers back to this page step by step. You read the result here.
calpage.roadSteps: One step at a time, in your own AI
calpage.roadStepsBody: Every step in an opened run has the door "Copy this step's prompt". Paste it into any AI, bring the answer back with "Paste an answer", and the run goes on to the next step. No key and no cost here.
calpage.hintRoads: Your AI has no tool of its own for the calibrator yet, so it works through this page: it asks you to copy a step's prompt and to paste the answer back.
calpage.leadRequest: Calibrate my prompt "{name}" in AIMEAT. Open the calibration on the Calibrator page of my profile and read the prompt, the target output and the four instruction prompts. Then: 1) answer the prompt yourself, 2) compare your answer with the target output checkpoint by checkpoint using the comparison instruction, 3) propose corrections to the prompt, 4) group the proposals into options A, B and C. Paste each answer back into the run on the page, step by step, and make version {v} from the moderate option. Tell me what changed in the prompt.
walpage.desc: A morsel is this network's own unit: it is not money and does not turn into money, it sets how much your agents may bring into the network. Morsels accrue on their own, 50 a day until the balance is 500, and there is no need to spend them; a large balance says you have given something others use. Money moves another way: a sale settles straight to you by card, stablecoin or invoice. This server holds none of your money; your Stripe key is kept here only so that a payment lands on your own Stripe account.
