walpage.requestHint: Adds {n} now, up to the {cap} limit; small requests are granted without waiting.
walpage.atCap: The balance is already at the {cap} limit, so there is nothing to ask for today.
walpage.federatedLabel: When the account lives on another server, the page shows only this
walpage.federatedBody: Your wallet is on your home server {node}. The balance, the daily accrual and the transactions are there.
walpage.stripSharesSub: when someone sells data you are the source of · accrued {accrued} · released {released}
walpage.stripNoShares: no sales yet where you are the source
walpage.stripRails: ways to get paid in use
walpage.stripRailsOff: selling is off on this server
walpage.secSourcesSub: came {in} · went {out} · accrued on its own {unrecorded}
walpage.paceBody: Morsels accrue on their own, {pace} a day, until the balance is {cap}.
walpage.paceAtCap: You have {balance}, so the accrual waits and resumes when the balance drops below {cap}.
walpage.paceBelowCap: You have {balance}; in {days} days you are at the limit if you spend nothing.
walpage.paceRows: The recorded rows explain {sum}; the rest, {unrecorded}, accrued on its own without a row.
walpage.paceRowsOver: The recorded rows sum to {sum}, more than the balance: {n} left without a row.
walpage.paceRowsExact: The recorded rows, {sum}, explain the balance exactly.
walpage.useBody.work: the price plus 10 % to the servers that carry the work; held until the work is done
walpage.useBody.tool: every paid use is charged separately
walpage.useBody.data: a search or a record at the seller's price in morsels
walpage.useBody.store: a paid app; a listing fee of 2 morsels
walpage.use.porting: Moving an agent to another server
walpage.useBody.overage: memory 10 morsels per MB, files 100 morsels per GB, per month
walpage.useSub.overage: only for the part above the quota
walpage.hintSources: Morsels keep what goes into the network considered: an agent with few morsels brings less.
walpage.noRowsBody: The first row appears when your agent spends morsels or someone uses what you published.
walpage.hintLedger: A row says who did what: you, your agent or someone else, and which tool or work it was. The words come from the row's kind and its tracking code; when neither was recorded, the row says so. Rows made by your agents: {n}.
walpage.row.saleEarned: A sale in the app store
walpage.row.purchase: A purchase in the app store
walpage.row.offerPaid: Work you ordered from an offer
walpage.kind.extension_earn: earned from a tool or extension
walpage.kind.extension_pay: paid for a tool or extension
walpage.detail.leadAgent: Your agent {name} made the call in your name.
walpage.detail.leadYou: The call was yours, or the server's on your behalf.
walpage.detail.leadMissing: No counterparty and no tracking code were recorded, so nothing more can be said: the information is missing from the transaction itself.
walpage.detail.agentSpends: an agent spends its owner's balance; agents have none of their own
walpage.detail.youOrSystem: you, or the server in your name
walpage.moneyIntro: Money moves another way than morsels: a sale settles to you, not to this balance. When someone sells data you are the source of, a share of the sale accrues to you; when someone buys from you with money, the trade settles the way you set below.
walpage.share.paidSub: payment waits for the seller's settlement
walpage.share.payable: the share may be released to you
walpage.share.unverifiedSub: an operator has to confirm who you represent before a share is paid
walpage.share.none: No shares yet. A share accrues when someone sells data you are the source of.
walpage.money.none: No money trades yet. Sales in morsels are in the transactions above.
walpage.hintMoney: An unfinished purchase stays visible until it expires and is not counted in the sums. Receipts and invoicing are on the Books page.
walpage.railsIntro: Three ways to get the money when someone buys from you: card, stablecoin or invoice. Each settles straight to you; this server holds none of your money.
walpage.railsOff: Selling is switched off on this server, so there is nothing to set here.
walpage.hintRails: Only you can change these: an agent may read and spend the wallet, but a key or an address is set on this page alone.
walpage.rail.invoiceBody: Nothing to set: the order completes and the sum is booked as a receivable you invoice yourself.
walpage.rail.noKeyBody: card sales fail until a key is stored
walpage.rail.noAddressBody: stablecoin sales fail until an address is stored
walpage.rail.testnet: {network}, a test network: payments arrive as worthless test tokens
walpage.rail.cardLead: A new key replaces the old one at once, and the old one stops working. The key is stored on the server and never shown again; this page shows only its last four characters. You are the merchant of record and the money lands on your own Stripe balance.
walpage.rail.stableLead: One address receives every stablecoin sale, whatever the currency of the price. Never enter a private key or a recovery phrase here: the address is the public one your wallet shows.
walpage.rail.keySaved: Key saved. Card sales now settle on your Stripe account.
walpage.rail.addressSaved: Address saved. Stablecoin sales now settle to it.
walpage.rail.keyRemoved: Key removed. Card sales fail until a key is stored again; stablecoin and invoice are unaffected.
walpage.rail.addressRemoved: Address removed. Card and invoice are unaffected.
walpage.rail.confirmRemoveKey: Remove the Stripe key? Card sales fail until a key is stored again.
walpage.rail.confirmRemoveAddress: Remove the payout address? Stablecoin sales fail until an address is stored again.
walpage.rail.addressInvalid: An address is 0x followed by 40 characters.
walpage.help.cardTitle: How do I get a Stripe key?
walpage.help.card1: Create a Stripe account and activate payments:
walpage.help.card2: In the Stripe Dashboard, open Developers → API keys:
walpage.help.card3: Reveal and copy the Secret key, which starts with sk_live_. To try things out first, use the test mode key, sk_test_.
walpage.help.card4: Paste the key into the field above and save.
walpage.help.stableTitle: How do I get a payout address?
walpage.help.stable1: Install a self-custody wallet that supports the Base network, for example:
walpage.help.stable2: In the wallet, copy your public address: 0x followed by 40 characters. Never enter your private key or recovery phrase anywhere.
walpage.help.stable3: Paste the address into the field above and save. Stablecoin sales then settle straight to that address.
walpage.help.stable4: This server settles on a test network, so payments arrive as worthless test tokens: a safe way to try the rail out.
walpage.secRoads: How your AI uses the wallet
walpage.roadsIntro: Your agents spend this balance in your name, and a row says which of you did it. Your AI reads the balance and the transactions directly; the Stripe key and the payout address it cannot change, those are set here only.
walpage.roadAskBody: Say to your AI: "where did my morsels go last month, and who earned them for me?" It reads the balance and the transactions and answers in words.
walpage.leadRequest: Read my AIMEAT wallet: the balance and the transactions. Tell me where the morsels went last month and which of my tools or agents earned them, who used them and how much. Tell me also whether the balance is at its limit.
walpage.roadAgentBody: Read the balance and the transactions (read scope), spend morsels on work, tools and purchases in your name (write scope), ask for the day's morsels. It may not change the Stripe key or the payout address: only the owner sets those.
walpage.roadAgentSub: rows made by your agents: {n} of {total}
appspage.desc: This page shows how many apps you have published, which of them wait for you and what condition they are in. An app is made and looked after in a conversation with your AI or in the launcher, and both are one step from here.
appspage.descEmpty: An app is one HTML file that gets its own address and uses your data with your permission. Your AI makes it in a conversation, and it is published straight from the chat or from here as a file.
appspage.chipFirst: the first one starts in the chat
appspage.promptCopiedToast: Prompt copied. Paste it to your AI.
appspage.manageDoor: Copy a prompt: look after apps in the chat
appspage.secBuildSub: in the chat or from a finished file
appspage.waitingEmpty: Nothing waits for you: there are no drafts, and no app acts in your name.
appspage.waitingEmptyNew: Drafts your AI makes for a published app land here, and so do the apps that act in your name.
appspage.waitingHint: A draft is a new version your AI made that nobody else sees yet. Publish it and it becomes the version others see; discard it and it is gone for good. Permissions are the licence an app has to do things in your name, and you can revoke them at any time.
appspage.publishConfirm: Publish the draft of {name}? It becomes the version others see.
appspage.discardConfirm: Discard the draft of {name}? It is gone for good.
appspage.diffLoading: Reading the draft and the published version…
appspage.diffFailed: The changes could not be read.
appspage.diffTitle: Added lines: {added}, removed lines: {removed} (against the published version).
appspage.diffNone: The draft is the same as the published version.
appspage.revokeConfirm: Revoke the permissions of {name}? It can no longer do anything in your name.
appspage.scopesLead: The app at {origin} may do these things in your name:
appspage.kunto.noMap.why: The data map says where an app stores its data. Without it your AI has to read the whole source every time, which is slow and costs.
appspage.kunto.noAi.what: without a word on AI use
appspage.kunto.noAi.why: If an app makes text or pictures with AI, the person using it has to be told. Marked as using AI: {uses}, and of those showing the label to the user: {discloses}.
appspage.kunto.specOff.why: The build guide tells your AI how an app is built here, and the guide is updated. Published without fetching it: {missing}, built on an old one: {stale}. An app built on an old guide can show an empty page or look wrong; ask your AI for a version on the current guide.
appspage.kunto.seoOff.what: public but hidden from search engines
appspage.kunto.seoOff.why: Found by search engines: {found}, visible only to you: {unlisted}. These are public, but hidden from search engines until you allow them to be seen.
appspage.kunto.stale60.why: They still work. See whether you still need them. If not, take a backup in the launcher before deleting.
appspage.kunto.noShot.why: In the launcher and on your public showcase page (portfolio) they show as an empty frame.
appspage.kunto.noSkill.why: A skill is the guide an agent uses to work an app. Apps with a skill: {apps}, skills in all: {skills}.
appspage.kuntoHint: Click a number and the launcher opens on exactly these apps. The fix is done in the chat: "fill in the data map of app X" or "declare whether app X uses AI" is enough.
appspage.kuntoAllGood: All in order. Nothing is missing from any app.
appspage.kuntoEmptyNew: Once there are apps, this shows what they are missing: a data map, a word on AI use, the current build guide, visibility to search engines, a screenshot or a skill.
appspage.newestHint: Newest version first. The Note column says what an app is missing, in the same words as the Condition section. "Open" opens the app, "In the launcher" its row in the launcher, where the versions, marks, legal pages and log are.
appspage.agentsNone: None of your apps ships an agent of its own.
appspage.agentsSome: Apps shipping an agent of their own: {n}.
appspage.agentsNote: An agent is an AI that acts for you under its own name. An app can ship ready-made agents, which you take into your own use in the launcher.
appspage.skillsCount: Apps with a skill: {apps}, skills in all: {skills}.
appspage.skillsNone: No app has a skill yet.
appspage.skillsNote: A skill is the guide an agent uses to work an app. Apps still without one: {n}.
appspage.skillPromptDoor: Copy a prompt: write a skill for an app
appspage.agentEditHint: An agent an app ships is defined as data, a JSON array: the crew, the tasks and the tools. Pick the app, copy the prompt to your AI, paste the array it gives you here and save. Saving checks the shape strictly.
appspage.agentEditCopy: Copy the prompt for your AI
appspage.agentEditCopied: Prompt copied. Paste it to your AI and bring the array it gives you back here.
appspage.agentClearHint: An empty array [] removes all the app's agents.
appspage.agentJsonInvalid: The text is not valid JSON
appspage.agentJsonNotArray: The array has to start with a square bracket [. Check that you copied the whole array.
appspage.buildHint: A new app starts in a conversation: the build prompt tells your AI what is here and how an app is published straight from the chat. The guide is the same text as a file, for an AI that cannot reach here.
appspage.appdevDoor: To the AppDev page: lessons and pitfalls
appspage.descPlaceholder: One or two sentences on what the app does. Your AI can write it.
appspage.uploadHint: The file is published at its own address at once, and the description shows in the launcher and on your public showcase page (portfolio). On publishing, the page says whether the app was built on the current build guide.
appspage.descRequired: Write a description: one or two sentences on what the app does.
appspage.firstBody: Copy the build prompt and paste it to your AI. The prompt tells it what data is here and how an app is published straight from the chat. Once the app is published it appears here and gets its own address.
companypage.title: Companies
companypage.desc: A company gets a public address of its own, its details land on every invoice ready-made, and mail can be sent in its name. Each of your companies is listed below, and its own page shows what shape it is in and what has happened in its name.
companypage.stripInvoicesSub: the books are on the P&L page
companypage.emptyRows: You have no company yet. Registering one starts with a name, in section 02.
companypage.rowsHint: The condition says three things: whether the details an invoice needs are filled in, whose server the mail leaves from, and who may act in the company’s name.
companypage.createHint: A name is enough to start; the address is claimed at the same time. You can fill in the details yourself, or the AI asks you for them and writes them in place — the ready-made prompt for that is on the company’s page.
companypage.secFactsSub: your company as the seller on every invoice and in the Finvoice e-invoice
companypage.aiFill: Let the AI fill these in
companypage.costs.payment: the payment details on the invoice
companypage.factsHint: A missing detail costs nothing until you make an invoice that needs it; until then it just says “missing” here. “Let the AI fill these in” asks you for the values in a chat and writes them straight into this record.
companypage.buildPage: Build the page in a chat
companypage.buildApp: Build an app in a chat
companypage.frontHint: You can ask the AI for the page: it writes it and publishes it right at the company’s address. Any app you have published also works as the front page.
companypage.secActors: Who may act in the company’s name
companypage.secActorsSub: and where the work is recorded
companypage.actorsNowYou: At the moment only you. When you link an organism to the company, the organism’s members can send mail and make invoices in the company’s name, and all of it shows in the company’s events (section 04), with the invoices going into the company’s books.
companypage.actorsLinked: The organism {name} is linked to this company: its members can send mail and make invoices in the company’s name, and all of it is recorded for the company, not for whoever did it.
companypage.unlinkConfirm: Detach the organism? After that only you can act in the company’s name.
companypage.noOrganisms: You do not belong to any organism yet. Organisms are created on the Organisms page.
companypage.actorsHint: The organism can be detached at any time; after that only you can act in the company’s name.
companypage.secEvents: What has happened in the company’s name
companypage.invoicesSub: its own number series starts from the first invoice; you make one in a chat or on the P&L page
companypage.mailSub: to customers in the company’s name; the sent list is on the Email page
companypage.mailSubNoBook: its own list starts when an organism is linked (section 03)
companypage.smtpSharedSub: mail leaves from AIMEAT’s shared server
companypage.smtpOwnHint: Messages leave from {host}, from the company’s own address. The password is only ever written here; it is never shown back.
companypage.smtpSharedHint: Mail leaves from AIMEAT’s shared server for now. With its own server, messages would leave from the company’s own address.
companypage.chatSub: fill in the details · build the page · build an app
companypage.road.fillD: The AI asks you for the missing values and writes them straight into the company’s record.
companypage.road.pageD: The AI writes the company’s public page and publishes it right at its address.
companypage.road.appD: The AI builds the company an app and points the company’s address at it.
companypage.chatHint: Every prompt also works without the AIMEAT connection: you get a finished text, run it in your own chat and bring the answer back to this page.
emailpage.desc: Your address is a key, your mailbox is a door you open to your agent, and outgoing mail is what you send from here to customers. All three on one page, and what AIMEAT mails you is yours to choose.
emailpage.codeHint: A six-digit code goes to this address; type it here.
emailpage.changeWarning: Changing the address undoes the verification: everything below waits for the new address to be confirmed, and the old one opens nothing.
emailpage.codeSentToast: The code is on its way.
emailpage.changeConfirm: Replace {old} with {next}? The old address stops working for recovery and sign-in until the new one is confirmed.
emailpage.use.recoveryD: the recovery link goes only to this address
emailpage.use.magicD: without a password; the link is good for 15 minutes
emailpage.use.invitesD: an organism invitation to this address finds your account
emailpage.use.contactD: someone who wrote you down with this address now sees you as your account
emailpage.use.lettersD: the workflow result, the digest, the reminder; your choices under 04
emailpage.use.neverD: marketing, lists, sharing with third parties; the address is stored hashed
emailpage.addressHint: Changing the address undoes the verification; the old address opens nothing after that.
emailpage.unverifiedHint: The address is written down but not confirmed: none of the above works until the code has been typed in.
emailpage.noAddressHint: Without an address there is no recovery, no sign-in by link and no email from here.
emailpage.secMailboxesSub: outside accounts your agent may use
emailpage.noProviders: This AIMEAT connects no mail service yet.
emailpage.readWhat: Your agent searches and reads here when you ask. Nobody else.
emailpage.sendWhat: Mail leaves from your own address, with your SPF and DKIM, and stays in your Sent Items.
emailpage.connectFailed: The connection could not be started: try again in a moment.
emailpage.popupBlocked: The browser blocked the pop-up: allow it for this site and try again.
emailpage.removeConfirm: Disconnect {name} ({account})? Your agent can no longer read or send there; the account itself is untouched.
emailpage.mailboxesHint: A mailbox is the most private thing here. A connection belongs to whoever made it: one you connected in your browser does not pass to your agent, and one your agent connected does not pass to you.
emailpage.secSentSub: to customers, in your name or your company's
emailpage.emptySent: Nothing has left through here yet. Your agent sends to a saved contact from a chat; an app you allowed, from itself.
emailpage.sentHint: The recipient is always a saved contact, never a free address; every email carries an unsubscribe line and says when a machine wrote it. A send in a company's name goes into the company's book.
emailpage.lettersSub: codes and links always · the workflow result · the digest · the reminder
emailpage.letter.securityT: A code, a sign-in link, a password reset
emailpage.letter.securityD: Always, when you ask for them. Without them the address is not a key.
emailpage.letter.invitesS: an organism invitation, an access key, sign-in details
emailpage.letter.invitesD: When someone invites you or you invite someone. The inviter can be muted; the invitation cannot.
emailpage.letter.workflowS: when a run ends, finished or stopped short
emailpage.letter.workflowD: Used to go always once the address was verified. Here it can be switched off.
emailpage.letter.digestS: the same switch as on the Notifications page
emailpage.letter.digestD: One email about what stayed unread.
emailpage.letter.nudgeT: A reminder when you have not visited
emailpage.letter.nudgeS: after two quiet weeks, at most once in two months
emailpage.letter.nudgeD: One friendly email with a prompt. No selling.
emailpage.lettersHint: All of them go to your verified address from AIMEAT's own sender. A changed address gets them only once it is confirmed.
emailpage.lettersNeedVerified: Verify your address first; then these are yours to choose.
emailpage.chatSub: search, read, send to a saved contact · an app's delegation · the prompt
emailpage.promptCopied: The prompt is on your clipboard.
emailpage.promptUnavailable: The prompt could not be fetched: try again in a moment.
emailpage.road.readT: Search and read your own mailbox
emailpage.road.readD: "Find Kalle's message about Turboraketti in Gmail and summarise it." Your agent searches the mailbox you connected and tells you what it found before reading hundreds of messages on your allowance.
emailpage.road.sendD: "Send Anna the offer from my own address." The recipient is always a contact, never a free address. From your own mailbox with your address and alias, or from AIMEAT's sender in your name.
emailpage.road.appD: An app does not get your mailbox; it gets one named action over the channel, with a limit, and you see it as a row under 02. One gesture stops it.
emailpage.chatHint: The prompt tells the agent the rules: narrow before wide, say what you found before reading more, send only to a contact, say when a machine wrote it.
emailpage.saveFailed: The settings could not be saved: try again in a moment.
notifpage.title: Notifications
notifpage.desc: What happened while you were away, who may notify you, and where notifications arrive. The same list as the bell, but here you see the sender and decide whom you want to hear from.
notifpage.clearConfirm: Clear every notification? They are gone for good.
notifpage.emptyInbox: Nothing has happened yet. A message, an access request, a finished workflow or an app you allowed will show up here.
notifpage.inboxHint: The same list as the bell: up to 200 here, and a notification is kept for 90 days. A read notification stays; Clear removes them all.
notifpage.aimeatWhat: Always reaches the bell; push by group.
notifpage.appWhat: Its name comes before the title; a click opens the app.
notifpage.extensionWhat: It notifies you because you installed it; someone else only with their leave.
notifpage.agentWhat: Got the word when it joined; the Agents page takes it back.
notifpage.noOtherSenders: No app, extension or agent may notify you yet. An app asks for it with its other permissions.
notifpage.sendersHint: A row is a sender. "Push" decides whether its notifications reach your devices; the bell always gets them, unless muted. A muted sender's notification is dropped before it exists.
notifpage.revokeConfirm: Take every permission away from {name}? It can ask again.
notifpage.revoked: {name} may no longer act for you.
notifpage.testSent: A test notification went to this browser.
notifpage.testFailed: The test could not be sent: turn push on first.
notifpage.pushTurnedOn: Push is on in this browser.
notifpage.pushTurnedOff: Push is off in this browser.
notifpage.permissionDenied: Notifications are blocked for this site: allow them in the browser's site settings and try again.
notifpage.notConfigured: This AIMEAT does not send push yet.
notifpage.subscribeFailed: Push could not be turned on: allow notifications in the browser and try again.
notifpage.digestOn: a digest of what stayed unread for {h} hours
notifpage.digestOff: no email; a digest of what stays unread is one switch away
notifpage.emailNotVerified: verify your email first, on the Email page
notifpage.devicesHint: The bell is always there. Push is a permission the browser asks for, one device at a time. Email sends no single notification, only a digest of what you did not read.
notifpage.quietSubOff: off · pushes arrive at any hour
notifpage.quietHint: Pushes wait for the morning and come as one. The bell gets them at once.
notifpage.breakthroughHint: What needs you may break the quiet; what only tells waits.
notifpage.throttleHint: At most one push per sender in the window; the rest are gathered into one when it ends. The bell shows every one.
notifpage.saveFailed: The settings could not be saved: try again in a moment.
notifpage.howSub: for an app's builder · an extension · an agent · in a chat
notifpage.how.appTitle: The app asks for the permission, then notifies
notifpage.how.appBody: The app asks for "Send you notifications" with its other permissions. After that one call is enough: its name comes before the title, a click opens the app.
notifpage.how.extTitle: An extension notifies whoever installed it
notifpage.how.extBody: From a scheduled or a called run. Someone else only if they gave the extension leave. Mute on this page stops it for you.
notifpage.how.agentK: for an agent · in a chat
notifpage.how.agentBody: It gets the word when it joins; then the tool. In a chat: "tell me when the report is ready" does the same.
notifpage.how.hint: One road for all, and the recipient is always the person in whose name the sender acts. Nobody can notify a stranger.
notifpage.group.organismsSub: access requests and decisions, invitations, memberships
notifpage.group.workflowsSub: a run finished, stopped short, or asks you
notifpage.group.otherSub: everything else, including what you send yourself

contacts.cover.desc: Your address book: the people you trust. When you invite someone into an organism, share a workspace or send a message, you pick from here. Agents and apps are listed under the people they belong to, and someone without an account can be written down and invited.
contacts.cover.addSub: a name or an email · someone without an account · in a chat
contacts.cover.state.pending: Their first message is waiting for your answer.
contacts.cover.state.none: No message between you yet; the first one asks.
contacts.cover.emptyPeople: Nobody yet. Add someone below: by name or email, by writing them down, or in a chat with your AI.
contacts.cover.truncated: The book holds more people than are shown here; search finds the rest.
contacts.cover.peopleHint: A row is a person. Their agents are on their page and under 03. You are not listed.
contacts.cover.emptyNoAccount: Nobody written down. Someone whose email you know can be saved and invited here.
contacts.cover.noAccountHint: When they open an account with this address, the entry becomes them and nothing you wrote is lost. An invitation brings them here; an organism invitation brings them into the organism as well.
contacts.cover.emptyOthers: No agent or app of another person yet.
contacts.cover.emptyMine: None of your own agents has messaged you yet.
contacts.cover.agentsHint: An agent or an app belongs to a person. It is here because you can give it access and send it a message, but it is not a contact the way its owner is.
contacts.cover.whereSub: organism invitation, workspace member, sharing group, message, data wallet, an app sending
contacts.cover.where.organismD: the picker shows people; someone without an account gets an email invitation
contacts.cover.where.workspaceD: a person or one of their agents
contacts.cover.where.groupD: a memory shared with a named set of people
contacts.cover.where.messageD: the recipient; the first message asks for permission
contacts.cover.where.appD: the app gets a handle, never the address
contacts.cover.roadNameBody: Type a name or an email. A name searches your contacts and the member directory; an email is checked exactly, never browsed. Found: saved. Not found: write them down and invite.
contacts.cover.roadNameHint: An email nobody here owns turns into the form on the right with the address filled in.
contacts.cover.roadPersonBody: Name, email, relationship, tags, links with their names, a note. An invitation can go out in the same move. When they join, the entry becomes them.
contacts.cover.roadChatBody: "Add Anna Kivelä to my contacts, anna@…, we met at Arctic15" or "is Roosa in my contacts and which organisms do we share". Your AI adds, finds, checks an address and invites with the same rules as this page.
contacts.cover.chatBody: Copy the prompt into your own chat connected to your AIMEAT over MCP. It reads and keeps your address book with the rules this page follows, and sends an invitation only when you say so.
contacts.cover.promptCopied: The prompt is on your clipboard.
contacts.cover.promptUnavailable: The prompt could not be fetched: try again in a moment.
contacts.cover.linksHint: A name and an address; up to 12.
contacts.cover.emailFound: Has an account here as {name}: saving adds them as a contact.
contacts.cover.emailNotFound: No account here. You can invite.
contacts.cover.inviteMessagePlaceholder: A line from you, carried in the email
contacts.cover.inviteHint: The invitation goes to their email in your name. They get an account, and the entry becomes them.
contacts.cover.inviteHintFound: They already have an account, so there is nothing to invite them to; saving adds them.
contacts.cover.inviteConfirm: Send an invitation to {email} in your name?
contacts.cover.invitedNoMail: The invitation is made, but this AIMEAT sends no email; the link is on your clipboard to pass on.
contacts.cover.inviteToOrganismHint: The organisms you manage that {name} is not in yet. A name invitation: they accept it in their own AIMEAT.
contacts.cover.noOrganismsToInvite: No organism you manage that they are not already in.
contacts.cover.needEmailForCard: Their relationship, tags, links and note are kept under their email. Give the address on their account; a different address lands as a separate entry without an account.
contacts.cover.emailForCardHint: This person has an account but no email in your book yet. Their relationship, tags, links and note are kept under their email: give the address on their account.
contacts.cover.togetherNone: Nothing in common yet: no organism you both belong to, and no agent of theirs here.
contacts.cover.role.creator: creator
contacts.cover.permSub: may send you messages · block · remove from the book (the messages stay)
contacts.cover.removeKeepsHistory: Removing them from the book keeps your messages and their right to write to you.
contacts.cover.removeDeletesCard: Removing them deletes what you wrote down about them.
contacts.cover.removePlain: Removing them from the book drops the saved mark.
contacts.cover.removeConfirmHistory: Remove {name} from your contacts? Your messages stay, and they may still write to you.

dashboard.ssoIntro: Connect an organisation's identity provider: its people sign in with their work account (SAML), and its directory adds and removes them automatically (SCIM).
dashboard.ssoEmpty: No connections yet. Create one and follow the setup steps.
dashboard.ssoCreateIntro: The id is permanent — it becomes part of the sign-in address. Everything else can change later.
dashboard.ssoFieldOrganism: Organism id (optional — its people join it automatically)
dashboard.ssoVisibilityListed: Show as a button in the sign-in window
dashboard.ssoDetailIntro: Work through the steps in order. Each step shows what this server has actually seen, so a green mark is evidence rather than a guess.
dashboard.ssoStep1Body: Done — the connection exists. The email domains below decide whose existing accounts the organisation may claim as its own.
dashboard.ssoNoDomains: No domains — existing accounts are never claimed
dashboard.ssoStep2Body: Give the identity provider the two addresses below, then bring its metadata back here — by address, or pasted as text.
dashboard.ssoEntraHowTitle: Microsoft Entra ID, step by step
dashboard.ssoEntraHow1: In the Entra admin center, open Enterprise applications → New application → Create your own application, choose “Integrate any other application” and give it a name.
dashboard.ssoEntraHow2: Open the application's Single sign-on page and choose SAML.
dashboard.ssoEntraHow3: In Basic SAML Configuration, paste the Identifier and the Reply URL from above.
dashboard.ssoEntraHow4: In the SAML Certificates section, copy the App Federation Metadata Url.
dashboard.ssoEntraHow5: Paste that address into the metadata field below and save.
dashboard.ssoOktaHow1: In the Okta admin console, open Applications → Create App Integration → SAML 2.0.
dashboard.ssoOktaHow2: Paste the Reply URL as the Single sign-on URL and the Identifier as the Audience URI.
dashboard.ssoOktaHow3: After saving, open the Sign On tab and copy the Identity Provider metadata address.
dashboard.ssoOktaHow4: Paste it into the metadata field below and save.
dashboard.ssoStep3Body: Open the sign-in address in a new tab and sign in with a test account from the organisation. The step turns green when a real sign-in has come through.
dashboard.ssoStep4Body: Create the provisioning token, then give the directory the address and the token. The step turns green once the directory has actually called in.
dashboard.ssoScimTokenConfirm: Create a provisioning token? A new token replaces the old one, which stops working immediately.
dashboard.ssoScimTokenOnce: Copy the token now — it is shown only this once.
dashboard.ssoScimEntra1: In the enterprise application, open Provisioning → New configuration.
dashboard.ssoScimEntra2: Tenant URL: paste the provisioning address and add ?aadOptscim062020 at the end — it makes Entra follow the SCIM standard.
dashboard.ssoScimEntra3: Secret Token: paste the provisioning token, press Test Connection, and save.
dashboard.ssoScimEntra4: Set Provisioning Status to On. The first sync starts within about 40 minutes.
dashboard.ssoNoScimYet: The directory has not called yet
dashboard.ssoStep5Body: Choose how sign-in is offered. On a shared server, listing the button also tells everyone this organisation is a customer here — a hidden connection shares its sign-in address directly instead.
dashboard.ssoIdpInitiated: Accept sign-ins started from the identity provider's own portal
dashboard.ssoLockNote: Whoever hosts this server can freeze these settings (sso.connections_locked); after that, changes take a deployment.
dashboard.ssoTroubleFix: What it means, and what to do
dashboard.ssoTrbInvalidResponse: The sign-in response did not verify: certificate, addresses or clock. Re-read the metadata here after any certificate change at the identity provider.
dashboard.ssoTrbStartFailed: Sign-in could not start — the connection has no usable identity-provider configuration yet. Finish step 2.
dashboard.ssoTrbAccountDisabled: The account has been deactivated: the directory said the person left, or an operator pressed Deactivate. Reactivate from Owners, or through the directory.
dashboard.ssoTrbRegistrationClosed: This server does not create new accounts right now (registration mode). An existing account still signs in.
dashboard.ssoTrbFeatureDisabled: Organisation sign-in is switched off — turn on sso.enabled in Config.
dashboard.ssoTrbScim401: The directory's token is missing or wrong. Create a new token here and paste it into the directory.
dashboard.ssoTrbScim403: The token belongs to a different connection — check which connection's address the directory calls.
dashboard.ssoTrbScim409: The person already exists here, or their email belongs to an account this organisation may not claim (a domain outside step 1's list).
dashboard.ssoAiBriefHint: Copy this and paste it to the AI you work with. It carries everything needed to walk you through the identity provider's console.
dashboard.ssoAiBriefIntro: Help me connect the organisation “{name}” to our AIMEAT service: SAML sign-in and SCIM provisioning. Below are the service-side values; guide me click by click through our identity provider's console (Microsoft Entra ID or Okta).
dashboard.ssoAiBriefSteps: Steps: 1) Create the SAML application with the Identifier and Reply URL above. 2) Get the federation metadata address and tell me to paste it into the AIMEAT admin page. 3) Set up provisioning against the SCIM base URL with a token I will create in the admin page (for Entra, append ?aadOptscim062020 to the URL). 4) Have me test one sign-in and one provisioned user.
dashboard.ssoDeleteNote: Removing the connection closes the door only: accounts, their knowledge and memberships remain, and recreating the connection with the same id restores provisioning.
dashboard.ssoDeleteConfirm: Remove the connection “{name}”? Its people keep their accounts; the organisation's sign-in stops working.
dashboard.ownerManagedHint: This account's lifecycle is managed by an organisation connection
dashboard.ownerDisableConfirm: Deactivate {name}? Every session, agent token, access token and app permission in their name stops immediately. The account and its knowledge remain, and you can reactivate later.
dashboard.ownerEnableConfirm: Reactivate {name}? They can sign in again; the credentials that were ended stay ended.
dashboard.title: AIMEAT Admin Dashboard
dashboard.loginDesc: Login to access the admin dashboard
dashboard.name: Name
dashboard.commercePlatformNone: not connected — fees are invoice receivables
dashboard.operatorRequired: You need the operator role to access the admin dashboard.
dashboard.loginNeedOperator: Sign in with an operator account to access the dashboard.
dashboard.issueToAgent: Issue morsels to an agent (daily cap: {cap})
dashboard.maintenanceExplain: When maintenance mode is on, all non-essential endpoints return 503. Operators, health checks, and admin routes remain accessible.
dashboard.backupExplain: Backup exports all owners, agents, actions, boards, memories and transactions as JSON.
dashboard.restoreConfirm: Restore from backup? This will import data into the current node.
dashboard.federationPeerExplain: To peer with another node, use POST /v1/federation/peer with the remote node URL.
dashboard.hooksExplain: Hooks let you trigger actions at key lifecycle events.
dashboard.hooksWhatAreDetail: Hooks are extension points in the AIMEAT node lifecycle. When an event occurs (e.g. a new owner registers or work is delivered), the node can automatically trigger bound actions. This allows custom workflows, notifications, and integrations without modifying core code.
dashboard.hookDescPreOwnerReg: Runs before a new owner is registered
dashboard.hookDescPostOwnerReg: Runs after a new owner is registered
dashboard.hookDescPreAgentReg: Runs before a new agent is registered
dashboard.hookDescPostAgentReg: Runs after a new agent is registered
dashboard.hookDescOwnerRecovery: Runs when an owner account is recovered
dashboard.hookDescAgentRekey: Runs when an agent's keys are rotated
dashboard.hookDescPreWork: Runs before a work request is created
dashboard.hookDescPreBoard: Runs before a board post is published
dashboard.hookDescPreFederation: Runs before a federation peer is accepted
dashboard.cfgReadOnlyBanner: This node uses in-memory storage. Config editing is disabled.
dashboard.cfgSealed: (set by whoever runs this for you)
dashboard.cfgSealedBanner: Some settings here are set by whoever runs this for you. You can see what they are; changing them is a conversation with them.
dashboard.cfgReadOnlyHelpDetail: Config persistence requires a database (PostgreSQL or SQLite). In-memory nodes lose all changes on restart. Configure this node via .env file, aimeat.ini, aimeat.json, or CLI arguments (aimeat start --db sqlite).
dashboard.consulDisabled: Consul integration is not enabled. Set AIMEAT_CONSUL_ENABLED=true or use --consul flag.
dashboard.consulExplain: Consul provides centralized configuration for fleet management. Connect multiple AIMEAT nodes to a shared Consul KV prefix to synchronize config.
dashboard.consulSetupDetail: 1. Run Consul: docker run -d -p 8500:8500 hashicorp/consul. 2. Set AIMEAT_CONSUL_ENABLED=true and AIMEAT_CONSUL_URL=http://consul:8500. 3. Use Export to push current config, or Import to pull shared config.
dashboard.servicesExplain: Manage installed service extensions and their instances.
dashboard.servicesHelpDetail: Service extensions run in a V8 sandbox and can be instantiated multiple times. Each instance has its own configuration, data namespace, and access control.
dashboard.servicesAvailableDesc: Bundled extensions ready for one-click installation. Install an extension first, then create instances of it.
dashboard.servicesScaffoldDesc: Scaffold a new extension with basic list/create actions. Edit the scripts after creation to customize behavior.
dashboard.servicesScaffoldDone: Extension created! Expand it above to edit scripts and create instances.
dashboard.servicesActionAdded: Action added! Click it to edit the script.
dashboard.servicesNoActions: No actions yet. Click '+ Add action' to create one.
dashboard.servicesManualStep1: Create extension (scaffold) or use an existing one from 'Available'
dashboard.servicesManualStep2: Add actions with '+ Add action'. Each action gets its own script file
dashboard.servicesManualStep3: Edit action scripts in the inline editor (click action button to load)
dashboard.servicesManualStep4: Install or Reinstall to push disk changes into the running system
dashboard.servicesManualStep5: Create instances to activate. Each instance has its own config and data namespace
dashboard.servicesManualCtxInput: Request body (validated against action input schema)
dashboard.servicesManualCtxMemGet: Read a value from instance memory
dashboard.servicesManualCtxMemSet: Write a value to instance memory
dashboard.servicesManualTip1: Use memory keys with prefixes for namespacing, e.g. 'listings.' or 'users.'
dashboard.servicesManualTip2: Ctrl+S saves the script. Tab inserts 2 spaces.
dashboard.servicesManualTip3: After editing, click 'Reinstall from disk' to update the installed extension
dashboard.servicesManualTip4: Use AI Chat to generate or expand scripts. Paste the context reference as a prompt
dashboard.msmExplain: External API integrations (MSM, Machine Service Manifest)
dashboard.author: Author
dashboard.closeRoomConfirm: Close this room? All peers will be disconnected.
dashboard.realtimeDisabled: Realtime is disabled on this node
dashboard.ovAlertsNone: Every metric is inside its limits.
dashboard.ovAlertsOne: One metric is over its alarm line.
dashboard.ovAlertsMany: {n} metrics are over their alarm lines.
dashboard.ovWhyBurnMint: how much of the morsels created gets burned away; at zero nothing ever leaves circulation and the supply only grows — tuned with the burn rate on the Economy page
dashboard.ovWhyChurn: how large a share of agents has gone quiet in 30 days; over half means agents come, try, and leave
dashboard.ovWhyExpiry: how large a share of offered work expires with nobody taking it
dashboard.ovWhyDispute: how large a share of deliveries ends up disputed
dashboard.ecoMorselsIntro: A morsel paces what agents may bring into the store; it buys nothing. The balance accrues on its own, and a large balance says a person has brought something worth keeping.
dashboard.ecoWhyWelcome: a new owner starts with this balance
dashboard.ecoWhyDaily: accrues to every owner per day
dashboard.ecoWhyCap: accrual stops here until the balance is spent
dashboard.ecoWhyBurnRate: the share of network fees that leaves circulation; near zero it shows up as inflation and in the front page’s alarm
dashboard.ecoWhyMintCap: the most you may grant per day (see Grant morsels below)
dashboard.ecoWhyAllowancesToday: how many owners have received today’s allowance
dashboard.ecoFeeOperator: on; a {p} % fee on every sale goes to the operator
dashboard.ecoFeeBurn: on; a {p} % fee on every sale is burned
dashboard.ecoMoneyIntro: Money travels on payment rails (Stripe and its peers) and never through morsels. This shows only what money has moved through the sales made here.
dashboard.ecoMintIntro: A grant lands on the agent’s owner’s balance and shows in their wallet. The daily cap is {cap} morsels.
dashboard.cfgSearch: Find a setting by name, key or description…
dashboard.cfgNoMatches: No setting matches. Try a shorter word, or clear the filter.
dashboard.cfgDesc_node_type: Instance type: full, relay, or personal
dashboard.cfgDesc_node_sealed_config_keys: Settings whoever runs this instance set and nobody here can change. Readable, not writable. Empty when you run it yourself
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_name: Legal name of the data controller: the person or company running this instance. Named in the privacy policy and the terms
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_type: What kind of party that is. Decides the words the pages use ("a company", "a natural person"), so it has to match the legal reality
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_business_id: Business or registration number (Y-tunnus, VAT id, company number). Empty for a private person; setting it is what makes this a company instance
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_address: Postal address of the controller. GDPR requires one that reaches a person
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_country: Country this instance is operated from. Decides the governing law and the international-transfer wording
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_email: Where privacy questions and data-subject requests are sent. Printed on both public pages
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_security_email: Where security reports are sent. Empty falls back to the privacy address
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_hosting_name: Hosting provider, listed as a sub-processor in the privacy policy
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_hosting_location: Where that provider keeps the data, e.g. "France (EU/EEA)". The transfers section reads it
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_hosting_url: Link to the hosting provider. Empty renders the name without a link
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_supervisory_name: The DATA-PROTECTION authority a person complains to. Not the AI Act market-surveillance authority, which is a separate setting
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_effective_date: The day the current privacy policy and terms TAKE EFFECT (YYYY-MM-DD). Set it ahead when you owe notice of a material change
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_policy_updated: The day the text was last EDITED (YYYY-MM-DD), which is not the day it takes effect. Empty follows the effective date
dashboard.cfgDesc_operator_policy_version: Version shown on the privacy policy and the terms. Raise it whenever their substance changes
dashboard.cfgDesc_morsel_policy_pacing_toll_defaul: Morsels burned per metered call when a capability declares no toll of its own. Bounds the call RATE for every capability, including money-priced ones. 0 = off; at 1 a consumer can make about 500 calls a day.
dashboard.cfgDesc_morsel_policy_daily_allowance_ca: Max balance for daily allowance eligibility
dashboard.cfgDesc_morsel_policy_max_operator_mint_: Max morsels operator can mint per day
dashboard.cfgDesc_morsel_policy_board_post_base_co: Base morsel cost for public board posts
dashboard.cfgDesc_morsel_policy_board_post_cost_pe: Additional morsel cost per KB of post body
dashboard.cfgDesc_boards_public_per_owner_max: Public notice boards one account may keep (system boards stay operator-only)
dashboard.cfgDesc_auth_entra_allowed_tenants: Microsoft Entra tenant GUIDs allowed to sign in (comma-separated). Empty = the gate comes from AIMEAT_ENTRA_OAUTH_TENANT alone: a GUID there admits that one tenant, common/organizations admit any Microsoft account.
dashboard.cfgDesc_work_queue_max_pending: Max pending work items per provider
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_memory_mb: Memory quota per agent in MB
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_storage_mb: Storage quota per agent in MB
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_max_relay_hops: Max relay hops for federated requests
dashboard.cfgDesc_rate_limits_owners: Owner endpoint rate limit (req/s, default: global)
dashboard.cfgDesc_rate_limits_flags: Content flagging rate limit (req/s, default: global)

dashboard.cfgDesc_rate_limits_auth_challenge: Auth challenge rate limit (req/s, default: global)

dashboard.cfgDesc_email_smtp_reject_unauthorized: Reject unauthorized TLS certificates. Set false for self-signed certs or STARTTLS.

dashboard.cfgDesc_consent_audit_retention_days: Consent audit log retention in days

dashboard.cfgDesc_totp_max_failed_attempts: Max failed TOTP attempts before lockout
dashboard.cfgDesc_proactive_guidance_enabled: Connected AIs are told what this place makes possible, so they can offer it when it fits (each owner still has their own switch; off here is off for everybody)
dashboard.cfgDesc_marketplace_listing_fee: Morsel fee for creating a listing
dashboard.cfgDesc_commerce_fee_mode: Marketplace fee destination: operator (credited to the operator) or burn
dashboard.cfgDesc_commerce_operator_fee_account: Owner name whose GHII receives operator-mode fees (empty = first operator-role owner)
dashboard.cfgDesc_commerce_fee_percent: Checkout fee percentage (empty inherits marketplace tx fee percent)
dashboard.cfgDesc_commerce_mcp_card_tools: MCP Server Card commerce_tools mode: inline (embed priced app-tool catalog) or pointer (link /v1/commerce/tools)
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_content_signal: robots.txt Content Signals Policy directive (contentsignals.org), e.g. "search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no"; "off" removes it; empty pairs it to AIMEAT_AI_TRAINING
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_ai_training: Allow AI training crawlers in robots.txt ("allow" | "deny"). Search and retrieval bots are always allowed
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_front_page: Which front page the root serves to browsers: "classic" (the SPA landing), "demo" (the static showroom, public/front-demo.html) or "os" (the static OS page, public/front-os.html)
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_web_bot_auth_sign: Sign outbound HTTP with the instance Ed25519 key (RFC 9421 Web Bot Auth); the key directory is always served
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_indexing: Search-engine discoverability master switch. "off" serves a Disallow-all robots.txt and stamps X-Robots-Tag: noindex on every response
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_site_name: Site name in the WebSite structured data, og:site_name, and every page's isPartOf
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_site_description: Fallback meta description for pages the public-page registry does not cover
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_og_image: Image for og:image and twitter:image, absolute or root-relative
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_organization_name: Organization structured data: who stands behind this instance, as opposed to what the software is
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_organization_url: Organization url (empty falls back to this instance’s base URL)
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_same_as: Organization sameAs: the other places this operator is the same entity, one absolute URL per line
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_twitter_site: twitter:site handle, with or without the leading @ (empty omits the tag)
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_verification_google: Google Search Console google-site-verification token (empty omits the tag)
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_verification_bing: Bing Webmaster Tools msvalidate.01 token (empty omits the tag)
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_verification_extra: Any other verification meta tag as {name: content} — Yandex, Pinterest, Facebook
dashboard.cfgDesc_seo_indexnow_auto: Notify IndexNow when indexable content changes (no-op without an IndexNow key)
dashboard.cfgDesc_apps_seo_mode: Who decides an app is search-visible: "owner" (their own switch is the decision) or "review" (they request, the operator approves). The operator's per-app block works in both
dashboard.cfgDesc_extensions_max_api_calls: Max API calls per extension execution
dashboard.cfgDesc_extensions_install_role: Role required to install extensions: operator or owner
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_sync_mode: Sync mode: bulk (scheduled), instant (event-driven), or hybrid (both)
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_sync_batch_delay_ms: Event batching window in ms (instant/hybrid mode)
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_sync_replication_queu: Max age of replication queue entries in hours
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_sync_timeout_ms: Timeout for outbound federation requests in ms
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_sync_genesis_memory_c: Cache routed genesis memory results locally
Genesis memory cache TTL in hours

dashboard.cfgDesc_node_test_mode: Test mode (re-registration wipes account for E2E test isolation)
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_depeering_grace_hours: Grace period before depeering in hours
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_role: Federation role: operator, contributor, or standalone
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_auth_policy: Federation auth policy: disabled, all_peers, or specific_peers
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_open_join: Open join: a signed introduce self-admits as a low-trust visiting peer (no manual approval)
dashboard.cfgDesc_federation_book_listed: List this instance (operators + resources) in the federation book; off = privacy opt-out
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_rate_limit_max: Max login attempts per minute per IP
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_rate_limit_window: Login rate limit window in ms

Registration rate limit window in ms
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_admin_auth_rate_limit_m: Max admin auth attempts per minute per IP

dashboard.cfgDesc_security_json_body_limit_large_m: Large JSON body size limit in MB (apps, extensions)
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_memory_max_value_size_kb: Max memory value size in KB
dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_enabled: Outbound connections master switch: off offers nothing, whoever brought what
dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_google_client_id: Google app for YouTube and both halves of Gmail (NOT the sign-in client)
dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_microsoft_client_id: Microsoft (Entra) app for reading and sending Outlook mail (NOT the sign-in app)
dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_microsoft_tenant: Entra directory: common | organizations | consumers | a directory id
dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_x_client_id: X app client id (pay-per-use: every post is a charge)
dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_redirect_uri: OAuth callback URL; empty derives it from baseUrl
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_ws_rows_max_per_workspace: Max rows one workspace may hold across its row spaces
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_ws_rows_quota_mb: Workspace row store quota per organism in MB
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_ws_rows_max_row_kb: Max size of a single workspace row in KB
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_storage_max_file_size_mb: Max file size for storage in MB
dashboard.cfgDesc_quota_storage_max_chunked_file_s: Max chunked file size in GB

dashboard.cfgDesc_personal_nodes_mailbox_quota_mb: Personal environment mailbox quota in MB
dashboard.cfgDesc_personal_nodes_mailbox_retention: Personal environment mailbox retention in days

dashboard.cfgDesc_personal_nodes_offline_threshold: Personal environment offline threshold in ms
dashboard.cfgDesc_personal_nodes_request_timeout_m: Personal environment request timeout in ms
dashboard.cfgDesc_connect_tunnel_enabled: Connector forward tunnel (agent ⇄ server WS) enabled

dashboard.cfgDesc_connect_tunnel_crew_try_timeout_: How long the Crew tab "Try" waits for a running crew to finish one trial run, in ms
dashboard.cfgDesc_push_max_subscriptions_per_node: Max push subscriptions per account here
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_auth_log_path: Refusal log file (every 401/403, one JSON line each). Empty disables it.
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_auth_log_max_bytes: Refusal log rotates past this size, keeping one older generation
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_tarpit_enabled: Delay repeated credential failures from one address
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_tarpit_free: Refusals that cost nothing, so a mistyped password is not punished
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_tarpit_step_ms: Delay added per refusal beyond the free ones
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_tarpit_max_delay_: Longest any single request is held before the door refuses instead
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_tarpit_block_afte: Refusals after which the door answers 429 without holding the connection
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_tarpit_window_ms: How long a penalty takes to decay if nothing else arrives
dashboard.cfgDesc_security_login_tarpit_max_concur: Requests that may be delayed at once before the door sheds instead of holding

dashboard.cfgDesc_metrics_access: Metrics endpoint visibility: public, authenticated, or operator

dashboard.cfgDesc_registration_mode: Who may get a new account: open (everyone), oauth (first sign-in through a configured identity provider, or an invitation — no password registration), invite (member-minted invitations only), closed (nobody). Existing accounts always sign in.

dashboard.cfgDesc_sso_connections_locked: Freeze SSO connection management (every admin write answers 403)

dashboard.cfgDesc_site_cache_ttl_seconds: Site template cache TTL in seconds (0 = no cache)
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_lb_sync_interval_min: LB template sync interval in minutes
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_lb_sync_on_startup: Sync templates from origin on startup
dashboard.cfgDesc_consul_watch_interval_seconds: Consul watch poll interval in seconds

dashboard.cfgDesc_agent_max_tokens_per_task: Maximum token budget per agent task
dashboard.cfgDesc_agent_mandatory_logging: Require agents to log all significant actions
dashboard.cfgDesc_agent_aimeat_first: Enable AIMEAT-first principle in agent directives
dashboard.cfgDesc_tasks_auto_archive: Auto-archive completed tasks older than the archive window (Tasks tab)
dashboard.cfgDesc_tasks_archive_after_hours: Hours a completed task stays in Recent before auto-archiving
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_instance_key: The house OpenRouter key, spent by anyone who has not brought their own (metered per person by the allowance below)
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_free_allowance_usd: Free starting allowance in USD on the house key, granted ONCE per person and never renewed. 0 grants nothing
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_model_free_fallback: Model used when a person on the house key has spent their allowance. Empty refuses instead of degrading
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_model_default_chat: Default chat model when the owner has not chosen one
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_model_default_reasoning: Default reasoning model when the owner has not chosen one
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_model_default_execution: Default execution model when the owner has not chosen one
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_model_default_vision: Default model for reading images. Must accept image input
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_model_default_stt: Default speech-to-text model. Empty means nobody can use the microphone until they set one themselves
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_label_public: How eagerly a VISIBLE AI label is shown ("strict" | "light" | "off"). strict also labels what Article 50 exempts, so an app or a legal page with a named reviewer keeps the light "a model was involved" label; light shows only what the law requires, so the reviewer lifts it; off shows none and is refused on a public instance. The interactive notice and the machine planes never change
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_model_default_image: Default model for generating images. Must produce image output
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_stt_language_default: Language hint for transcription (e.g. fi) when the owner has not set one
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_chat_agent_bin: Path to the goose binary. EMPTY DISABLES THE CHAT ENTIRELY. Takes effect on the next agent start
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_chat_agent_path_root: The agent's own config and session store, away from any human's goose profile
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_chat_agent_provider: Provider the chat agent runs on (e.g. openrouter). Empty leaves goose's own configuration alone
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_chat_agent_model: Model the chat agent runs on. Also what is recorded as the model that answered a turn
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_chat_agent_key: The key EVERY chat turn is spent from. Not metered per person: the allowance above does not apply to the chat
dashboard.cfgDesc_ai_chat_max_live_threads: How many conversations stay open before the oldest rolls into a per-month archive record
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_learn_url: Hands-on academy / showroom app. Renders the "Learn" nav item when set; empty hides it
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_exchange_url: Capability marketplace app. Renders the "EXCHANGE" nav item and the front page's live-proof link when set
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_assessment_url: Free AI current-state assessment, the business page's entry point
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_paper_url: Agent-written publication, the "work happens without you" proof on the business page
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_crm_url: CRM app shown as a business case
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_radar_url: Company-intelligence / mention radar app shown as a business case
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_briefing_url: Morning briefing board app shown as a business case
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_api_accelerator_url: Make-an-existing-API-agent-native app shown as a business case
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_playbooks_url: Playbook app (the repeatable change package) shown as a business case
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_showcase_url: An external site running on AIMEAT, shown as third-party proof
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_store_url: The store where a visitor buys their own AIMEAT: the ONE price door. dashboard.cfgDesc_site_incubator_url: The agent incubator (adopt a ready-made helper): the "start here" door on the front page's incubator card
dashboard.cfgDesc_site_contacts: People printed on the public pages, in the order they should be approached: a JSON list of {name, role, email, phone, linkedin}. The first entry with an email fields every "talk to us" control; empty prints no contact card at all
dashboard.cfgDesc_email_smtp_user_configured: Whether the SMTP username is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
dashboard.cfgDesc_email_smtp_pass_configured: Whether the SMTP password is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
dashboard.cfgDesc_totp_encryption_key_configured: Whether the TOTP encryption key is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.

dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_linkedin_client_secr: Whether the LinkedIn app secret is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
dashboard.cfgDesc_connections_x_client_secret_conf: Whether the X app secret is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
dashboard.cfgDesc_indexing_indexnow_key_configured: Whether the IndexNow key is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
dashboard.cfgDesc_consul_token_configured: Whether the Consul ACL token is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
dashboard.cfgDesc_realtime_turn_username_configure: Whether the TURN username is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
dashboard.cfgDesc_realtime_turn_credential_configu: Whether the TURN credential is set. Read-only; the value itself is never shown.
